question: The world: how do the other jurisdictions do it?
answer: The International Crypto Map reads 22 jurisdictions on 13 dimensions each, from who has authority to who bears a loss; 191 of the 286 cells are researched, 85 partial and 10 still open. 7 of its 14 issuer records are live under a local license, 15 cross-border routes were reviewed and none is yet a recurring end-to-end corridor in the record, and most systems still finish in an existing bank or central-bank record.

groups.title: United States: 13 dimensions, 16 clocks, 11 gaps
groups.intro: The United States remains an active but unfinished federal stack, not one comprehensive crypto regime. The post-22 September record is material: the Federal Reserve proposed its GENIUS application and prudential rules; SEC and CFTC staff issued implementation guidance under existing authority; SEC filed an alleged $15 million cross-border crypto-fraud action; The Clearing House selected the technology for a future bank-token network; and Bridge launched OUSD across four public networks. These are different clocks. Proposed rules are not effective rules, staff FAQs are not Commission or statutory permissions, a complaint is not an adjudication, a vendor selection is not network launch, and a live stablecoin does not prove its reserve sufficiency or redemption performance. Incumbent bank, securities and central-bank settlement records remain authoritative within their scopes.

rows.title: Authority
cells: Congress and the executive define federal statutes and policy; Treasury, FinCEN and OFAC govern financial-crime and sanctions functions; the federal banking agencies govern institution-specific bank and stablecoin capacities; the SEC and CFTC retain object- and activity-specific market authority; the Federal Reserve and Reserve Banks govern account access and central-bank payment services; states retain material licensing, trust, money-transmission and commercial-law roles.
Policy, legislation, rulemaking, chartering, licensing, account access, supervision, enforcement and transaction operation are separate federal and state capacities.

rows.title: Legal objects
cells: The existing stack separates payment stablecoins, bank deposits including tokenized deposits, securities and security entitlements, digital commodities, derivatives, pooled vehicles, native cryptoassets and nonfungible objects. GENIUS excludes qualifying tokenized deposits from its payment-stablecoin definition and gives permitted payment stablecoins defined treatment without making every digital asset the same legal class.
Crypto is a technology and market label, not a single controlling federal legal object.

sources.label: SEC-CFTC Memorandum of Understanding and Joint Interpretation

rows.title: Permitted activities
cells: Issuance, exchange, transfer, custody, brokerage, dealing, payments, derivatives, fund activity and tokenized-security servicing remain governed by the exact object, actor and jurisdiction. The SEC's temporary conditional order permits a bounded Tokenized Securities Venue and liquidity-provider model for tokenized NMS stocks; GENIUS creates a separate future route for payment-stablecoin issuance. Neither supplies one universal permission for all crypto activity.
An approval, registration or exclusion for one object or activity cannot be borrowed by another affiliate, product, venue, chain or transaction.

sources.label: SEC-CFTC Memorandum of Understanding and Joint Interpretation

rows.title: Entry gates
cells: Entry may require an exact federal or state charter, stablecoin-issuer approval, money-transmission or trust authority, securities or commodities registration or scoped exemption, AML and sanctions controls, product or venue approval, and separate Federal Reserve account and service onboarding. The Federal Reserve proposed application procedures for Board-supervised issuers and specified state-qualified issuers; those procedures remain proposals and do not identify an approved applicant. The SEC order, OCC preliminary charter decisions, CFTC prerule review and TCH network plan operate at different gates; none establishes a generally operating firm or comprehensive regime.
Application, conditional approval, final approval, consummation, account grant, technical connection and first use are separate gates.

rows.title: Named operating actors
cells: The existing owners identify the Federal Reserve and Reserve Banks, Treasury, SEC, CFTC, OCC, FDIC, NCUA, FinCEN, OFAC, DTC and DTCC alongside exact issuers, custodians, banks, exchanges, wallets, processors and networks. The September OCC decisions add proposed Agora and Catena trust-bank legal persons at the preliminary conditional charter stage. Bridge Building Inc. is the identified OUSD issuer within the Bridge/Stripe group; BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY have stated reserve roles; Coinbase, Mastercard/BVNK, Stripe and Visa are distribution or integration paths rather than the token debtor. The Clearing House and Quant are future network operator and technology-provider roles, not deposit issuers for each member bank. The deeper Crypto Infrastructure Hub owns the entity and relationship graph.
A consumer brand, parent, affiliate, token administrator, reserve custodian, platform operator and legal issuer may be different persons.

rows.title: Claims and backing
cells: GENIUS payment stablecoins are private issuer liabilities backed by eligible reserve assets and a statutory redemption framework; the Act does not make them federally insured or government-guaranteed dollars. The Federal Reserve's proposed prudential rule would require covered issuers to maintain fair-value reserves at least equal to outstanding issuance at all times, calculate the position daily as of 5 p.m., remediate deficiencies within 24 hours, and meet a proposed two-business-day redemption standard. A tokenized bank deposit remains a bank-deposit claim. A DTC token is a controlled representation inside DTC's entitlement architecture rather than native bearer title to the underlying security. OUSD is a Bridge-issued stablecoin whose launch page names BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY reserve roles; the first promised monthly attestation had not yet been published.
Reserve assets, issuer liability, holder priority, deposit insurance, custody and central-bank money are different property and protection layers.

sources.label: Implementing the Federal Reserve Board's responsibilities under the GENIUS Act

rows.title: Domestic rails
cells: Fedwire Funds, FedNow, NSS, ACH, CHIPS, DTC, NSCC and FICC supply distinct money, clearing, securities and collateral functions. FedNow provides 24/7 final central-bank-money settlement under its rules, but no reviewed official record made it a general securities-DVP, CCP-margin, crypto-transfer or stablecoin-redemption rail. DTC token state, authoritative entitlement, clearing and the cash leg can occur on different systems and clocks.
Continuous instruction or token state does not prove continuous cash, securities-title, clearing or accounting finality.

rows.title: Cross border routes
cells: U.S.-linked stablecoins, card settlement, correspondent banking, Swift and public networks create cross-border dependencies, while GENIUS adds future foreign-issuer comparability, registration and lawful-order conditions. The existing country evidence does not establish one end-to-end production corridor with reconciled origin, FX, token, bank-payout, beneficiary-finality and loss records.
Global availability or an intermediary connection is not a sourced bilateral corridor or proof of final beneficiary receipt.

rows.title: Operating state
cells: GENIUS is enacted but delayed-effective, with Federal Reserve prudential and application rules now proposed rather than final. OUSD is technically live on four public networks, but its first monthly attestation and reconciled supply are pending. DTC has completed limited-production tokenization activity; FedNow and incumbent settlement systems are live; the SEC tokenized-securities exemption is temporary and conditional; CFTC AF80 remains at pending prerule review; the Agora and Catena charters remain preliminary conditional approvals; and TCH's On-Chain Money Initiative remains targeted for first-half 2027 availability. CLARITY has not become law and the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve lacks a publicly reconciled operating inventory.
Enacted, exemption-issued, prerule-reviewed, preliminary chartered, final-approved, opened, limited production, generally available and publicly reconciled operation are different states.

rows.title: Scale
cells: DTC disclosed July 15 limited-production workflows involving more than 30 firms, while the deeper Hub carries product- and actor-specific issuance, transaction and network metrics. Open Standard reports more than 200 OUSD partners and more than USD1 billion of near-term liquidity commitments, but those are neither outstanding supply nor funded reserves. The existing country synthesis does not yet reconcile a national entity-level census, legal-entity market shares, custody assets, stablecoin circulation by governing issuer or persistent tokenized collateral use.
Participant count, token supply, transaction value, custody assets, revenue, market share and systemic exposure are separate measures.

sources.label: Open Standard company structure and leadership

rows.title: Stress
cells: Statutes, proposals, operator rules and issuer terms allocate controls and remedies. The SEC's 29 September complaint adds an alleged USD15 million WhatsApp-led crypto investment fraud and asset-freeze request, but it is not an adjudicated platform insolvency, issuer failure or recovery distribution. The normalized country record still lacks a complete observed stress table for stablecoin redemption, custodian or bank failure, chain outage, exchange insolvency, tokenized-entitlement divergence or continuous-clearing liquidity gaps.
A reserve rule, risk control, simulation or contractual remedy is not evidence that the system performed as intended during a real failure.

sources.label: SEC charges multiple entities in alleged USD15 million crypto fraud schemes

rows.title: Correction and loss
cells: GENIUS supplies redemption, reserve, holder-priority and lawful-order mechanisms without federal insurance or guarantee. DTC and payment-system rules allocate authoritative-record correction and finality within their own scopes. Securities, custody, insolvency, forfeiture, sanctions and state commercial-law remedies remain object- and entity-specific.
Freeze or burn capability, operational reversal, restitution, insolvency priority, deposit insurance and sovereign backstop are not interchangeable remedies.

sources.label: Establishment of the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and United States Digital Asset Stockpile

rows.title: Evidence boundary
cells: This projection combines the August federal claim audit, settlement-control map, July GENIUS control plane and September Crypto Infrastructure Hub with a bounded federal refresh through 1 October 2026 at 13:25:37 EDT. It adds proposed Federal Reserve implementation, SEC and CFTC staff guidance, an alleged fraud case, OUSD launch and TCH network design. It remains incomplete on state law, final GENIUS rules, issuer approvals, final OCC opening decisions and Federal Reserve access, public CFTC AF80 text, actual use of the SEC exemption, OUSD reserve and redemption performance, corridor evidence and observed failure results.
Later final rules, legislation, approvals, first transactions or official inventories may change the United States record; the deeper owners remain controlling.

groups.title: United Kingdom: 13 dimensions, 8 clocks, 5 gaps
groups.intro: The United Kingdom has a live but partial crypto perimeter: money-laundering registration and financial-promotion rules are current, while the broader FSMA activity, custody, prudential, admissions and market-abuse regime remains scheduled for 25 October 2027. The material post-baseline change is that the FCA authorization gateway opened at 09:00 on 30 September 2026 and is scheduled to close at 23:59 on 28 February 2027. Opening accepts applications; it neither authorizes an applicant nor commences the future regime. Existing FSMA firms generally seek a variation of permission, other firms seek authorization, and the saving or runoff treatment depends on timely application and current status. Retail access remains concentrated at a small number of mostly overseas-facing brands, while applicant identity, determinations, legal-entity market share, custody assets, settlement finality and solvency remain unproved.

rows.title: Authority
cells: Parliament and HM Treasury define the statutory perimeter and commencement; the FCA registers the current AML population and will authorize and supervise in-scope firms under the future FSMA regime.
FCA research, registration, rulemaking, authorization and supervision are different acts and clocks.

sources.label: Description of the UK Cryptoasset Market

rows.title: Legal objects
cells: The regime distinguishes qualifying cryptoassets and activities, stablecoin-related issuer and redemption questions, and specified-investment cryptoassets whose custody treatment may follow CASS 6 rather than the new CASS 17 rules.
Token technology does not determine whether the legal object is a cryptoasset, security, fund interest, payment claim or property right.

rows.title: Permitted activities
cells: The future perimeter addresses offering or issuance, admissions, qualifying trading platforms, dealing and arranging, custody, lending, borrowing and staking. Present MLR registration does not grant all of those permissions.
A published future activity rule is not a current permission or firm-specific authorization.

rows.title: Entry gates
cells: MLR registration and financial-promotion compliance are current gates. The FCA's new-regime authorization gateway opened at 09:00 on 30 September 2026 and is scheduled to close at 23:59 on 28 February 2027, with the broader regime expected to commence 25 October 2027. Existing FSMA firms generally apply to vary permission; other firms apply for authorization. Timely applicants may rely on the applicable saving provision while pending, whereas late applicants are limited to transition or runoff and may not enter new contracts.
Application, determination, authorization and commencement must remain separate. Existing payments, e-money, MLR or FSMA status does not automatically confer the new permissions.

groups.title: Japan: 13 dimensions, 10 clocks, 8 gaps
groups.intro: Japan's digital-money record is a layered extension of incumbent legal claims rather than a new sovereign-money successor. The FSA's 30 September On-Chain Finance Forum adds a national roadmap process covering stablecoins, tokenized deposits, wallets, DEX/DeFi, JGBs and possible on-chain use of Bank of Japan current-account money, while a fourth PIP project links future three-megabank stablecoin payments to trade documents. These are coordination and experiment clocks, not production settlement. XRP Asia's 3 October launch adds Tokyo as a regional XRPL community node, but it is separate from the older SBI Ripple Asia joint venture and changes no Japanese licence, product or settlement state. JPYSC remains a live but closed-loop trust-beneficiary claim, and its lending service creates a separate unsecured repayment claim against SBI VC Trade outside customer-asset segregation. DCJPY remains issuing-bank deposit money; retail CBDC and tokenized BOJ reserves remain pilots. BOJ-NET remains the decisive wholesale yen-finality point unless a later legal and technical record proves otherwise.

rows.title: Authority
cells: The Diet and Cabinet define the legal perimeter; the FSA supervises cryptoasset, electronic-payment-instrument and banking actors and now convenes the interministerial On-Chain Finance Forum; the BOJ operates central-bank settlement and retail- and wholesale-money experiments; MOF owns sovereign-debt questions and retains a role with the Diet in any future retail-CBDC constitution.
Supervision, system operation, pilot work and sovereign issuance authority are different capacities.

rows.title: Claims and backing
cells: JPYSC is a specified-trust beneficiary claim backed by trust assets and is neither legal tender, a bank deposit nor deposit-insured. The 30 June snapshot disclosed ¥10,008,294,794 issued and ¥10,008,304,794 in the trust's deposit account. When a customer lends JPYSC to SBI VC Trade, that customer instead holds an unsecured consumption-loan repayment claim outside customer-asset segregation. DCJPY is an issuing-bank deposit backed by the bank's balance sheet. A future retail CBDC or tokenized BOJ current-account balance would be a BOJ claim only if legally and operationally issued.
Trust segregation, an intermediary loan claim, commercial-bank deposit insurance and a direct central-bank liability are different protections and failure paths.

The October recertification adds the forum and roadmap, Coincheck registration, PIP-4, exact JPYSC scale, lending-loss transformation, 43-bank experiment population and BOJ wholesale sandbox. Open questions include current reserve composition, open-wallet use, selected cross-bank settlement model, production cross-border reversal, observed digital-claim failure, exact replaced reporting templates and measured burden outcomes.

groups.title: South Korea: 13 dimensions, 12 clocks, 8 gaps
groups.intro: South Korea still had no enacted general public-won stablecoin regime at the cutoff. The material change is more specific: revised VASP entry and AML controls added reporting for transfers of at least KRW 10 million to overseas VASPs or personal wallets; enacted security-token statutes are being implemented for 4 February 2027 while stablecoin-linked payment remains a later phase dependent on pending legislation; and the H1 2026 regulator survey shows sharp declines in holdings, trading, deposits and profit despite a nearly flat eligible-account count. XRP Asia's 3 October launch adds Seoul as a regional XRPL community node and organizational hub activity, but the launch session and adjacent bank panel do not establish an XRP Asia bank partnership, XRPL deployment or XRP route. The Bank of Korea separately documented empirical stablecoin/FX transmission abroad but not the same significant linkage in Korea, and its annual systems report confirms that BOK-Wire+ central-bank money, not a token pilot, remains the final settlement anchor.

rows.title: Authority
cells: FSC sets financial policy; KoFIU owns VASP notification and AML/CFT controls; FSS supervises and joined the market survey; BOK owns central-bank-money and payment-system responsibilities; the finance ministry owns material FX policy; and KRX and KSD operate securities infrastructure. Security-token Acts are enacted for 4 February 2027, but subordinate rules were only proposed and general public-won-stablecoin legislation remained pending.
Policy ownership, VASP notification, a proposed implementing rule, an enacted-but-not-effective statute and operating-system control are distinct forms of authority.

A deposit token is the issuing bank's liability; a public stablecoin would be the exact issuer's liability; a security token represents securities rights; none is automatically a BOK liability.

groups.title: Indonesia: 13 dimensions, 10 clocks, 7 gaps
groups.intro: Indonesia now has a measurable OJK-supervised crypto stack: two exchanges, two clearing/guarantee/settlement institutions, two custodians and 27 licensed dealers at the August supervisory cutoff, serving 22.93 million accounts and IDR 20.52 trillion of July spot transactions. PT Adhyoka Berkah Maju's IDRP rupiah-stablecoin business model passed the OJK sandbox on 11 June, but no reviewed record establishes an issuer licence, public launch, reserves, redemption or lawful payment use. Bank Indonesia still separates crypto trading from legal rupiah payment, while Bank Mandiri, BRI, BNI, BCA and other banks scale conventional QRIS/account-money corridors. Digital Rupiah remains an experimental future central-bank claim, not production money.

rows.title: Authority
cells: OJK took crypto and digital-financial-asset supervision from Bappebti on 10 January 2025 and now licenses exchanges, clearing/guarantee/settlement institutions, custodians and dealers under POJK 27/2024 as amended by POJK 23/2025. Bank Indonesia retains currency, payment-system, FX, QRIS, BI-FAST/RTGS and Digital Rupiah authority; PPATK and enforcement bodies retain AML and crime-response functions.
OJK trading or sandbox authority does not authorize a payment instrument or central-bank liability; BI payment authority does not license a crypto dealer.

rows.title: Legal objects
cells: The regime separates traded digital financial assets and cryptoassets, digital-asset derivatives, dealer cash entitlements, segregated commercial-bank deposits, custodied cryptoassets, a sandbox-tested rupiah stablecoin model, bank/e-money rupiah balances and experimental Digital Rupiah. BI says Digital Rupiah would be a direct central-bank claim and is neither crypto nor stablecoin.
A QR credential, bank deposit, cryptoasset, sandbox stablecoin and CBDC are different legal objects; reference to rupiah does not make a private token legal tender.

rows.title: Permitted activities

Payment providers process rupiah account and QR payments. Stablecoin issuance has a passed sandbox model but no retrieved issuer licence; virtual-currency payment processing remains prohibited. Staking, lending and each tokenized-asset permission still require activity-specific confirmation.
Exchange listing, sandbox passage, dealer licence, custody, derivatives trading and payment use are separate permissions.

groups.title: European Union: 13 dimensions, 14 clocks, 10 gaps
groups.intro: The European Union is a supranational legal and supervisory layer, while the Eurosystem owns euro central-bank money and national law still controls important authorization, property and insolvency outcomes. MiCA is effective and the maximum grandfathering period ended by 1 July 2026. EBA counted 39 e-money tokens issued under MiCA and zero authorized asset-referenced tokens as of 1 September. SG-FORGE publishes live EUR and USD e-money-token circulation and reserve composition; BBVA Spain operates bitcoin and ether trading and custody. By contrast, the 37-bank Qivalis consortium says its proposed issuer is still awaiting Dutch authorization and does not issue e-money or provide public payment services. EBA and ESMA's late-September MiCA-review submissions are recommendations, not amended law. Pontes launched with onboarded participants, but no first completed transaction was found; Project Agorá used real value in a controlled test but moved ordinary bank deposits through existing core systems rather than launching a common production token.

rows.title: Authority
cells: The Parliament and Council legislate, the Commission administers and proposes revisions, EBA and ESMA coordinate and exercise assigned functions, national competent authorities authorize and supervise exact entities, and the ECB and national central banks govern euro central-bank money and TARGET Services. The Commission's MiCA consultation closed on 30 September, while EBA and ESMA submitted review recommendations; none amended MiCA at cutoff.
EU legislation, agency advice, national authorization, prudential supervision and Eurosystem settlement authority are separate layers and clocks.

groups.title: Singapore: 13 dimensions, 24 clocks, 17 gaps
groups.intro: Singapore uses overlapping activity- and rights-based regimes rather than one crypto licence. The dedicated MAS single-currency-stablecoin framework was still under legislative consultation and had not produced an issuer licence or MAS-regulated-stablecoin label at the cutoff. The bank operating layer is already material: DBS, OCBC and UOB completed live domestic SGD transactions using their own tokenized-deposit obligations with Swift's blockchain ledger matching and netting before final settlement through existing systems; DBS/Citi and UOB/HSBC also completed live cross-border USD and HKD routes. These are commercial-bank liabilities, not MAS money or a common stablecoin. DBS separately reports material crypto trading and trust inflows, while OCBC has live tokenized securities and a public-chain gold-fund token. groups.title: Australia: 13 dimensions, 11 clocks, 12 gaps
groups.intro: Australia's existing-law transition reached an enforcement hinge on 30 September: ASIC reported more than 45 digital-asset-related licence applications, but applications are not licences, and firms needing authority that did not satisfy the no-action conditions risk breach from 1 October. The future DAP/TCP regime remains enacted but uncommenced. On 30 September ANZ, BHP, Citi and Swift also completed a live Melbourne-New York USD corporate-treasury transaction using tokenized deposits behind BHP's ordinary ANZ account channel. This is stronger than Project Acacia's bounded research but does not disclose value, final-system records, recurring volume or exceptions. CBA, NAB and Westpac remain at different proof, working-group and product states. RITS Exchange Settlement Account entries remain the production final-money anchor; no clear public-interest case for retail CBDC has been established.

Legislation, financial-services licensing, AML registration, prudential supervision, payment-system operation and tax treatment are different capacities.

groups.title: New Zealand: 13 dimensions, 16 clocks, 8 gaps
groups.intro: New Zealand still has no single bespoke cryptoasset licence or general stablecoin statute, but the FMA's ECDD-specific designation has created a live, conditional legal perimeter for NZDD issued after 11 March 2026. Each NZDD is issued for NZD 1, backed by ECDD as trustee holding NZD in a bare-trust account at a registered bank, and redeemable by an eligible account holder subject to agreed restrictions; the token is declared not to be an FMC Act financial product only while full-backing, monthly publication and annual independent-verification duties are met. That is issuer-specific relief, not bank money, DCS coverage, central-bank money or approval of every NZD stablecoin. The four D-SIBs—ANZ New Zealand, ASB, BNZ and Westpac New Zealand—and Kiwibank remain dominant conventional deposit and payment institutions; the bounded bank-primary pass found no New Zealand-bank stablecoin, transferable deposit token, crypto custody product or production tokenised-settlement route. Australian-parent pilots cannot be attributed to their New Zealand subsidiaries. RBNZ's 28 September strategy folds Digital Cash into payments modernisation but leaves it unissued in Stage 2; ESAS and NZClear remain the production finality anchors.

rows.title: Authority
cells: Parliament and MBIE own the financial-markets, registration and consumer statutes; FMA applies conduct, product, market and specified licensing law; Companies Office operates the FSPR; DIA is the sole AML/CFT supervisor; Police FIU receives reports; Inland Revenue applies tax and CARF; RBNZ stewards money, operates ESAS and NZClear, supervises deposit takers and administers the DCS; RBNZ and FMA share most FMI regulation.
Registration, financial-product regulation, market licensing, AML supervision, tax reporting, prudential supervision, system operation and failure compensation are different capacities.

rows.title: Legal objects
cells: The record separates an AML/CFT virtual asset; an FMC Act debt, equity, managed-investment or derivative product; a financial service such as value transfer or means-of-payment issuance; an NZDD token issued by ECDD; ECDD's bare-trust interest for the token holder; the trust account's call debt security issued by a registered bank; an ordinary protected bank deposit; a proposed RBNZ Digital Cash liability; and a production ESAS balance.

NZDD, its redemption right, the bare-trust reserve, the registered bank's deposit liability, the token holder's position, DCS protection, a future RBNZ liability and ESAS central-bank money are not one legal object.

rows.title: Permitted activities
cells: Crypto exchanges and wallets may provide value-transfer services; issuers may issue or manage means of payment; tokens with regulated rights may be offered or serviced under the FMC Act; and VASPs may conduct exchange, transfer, custody, broking or token activities subject to applicable registration, fair-dealing, DRS and AML/CFT duties. ECDD may issue post-commencement NZDD within the exact designation conditions. Direct fiat subscription is limited by issuer terms to verified wholesale investors and direct redemption currently carries a stated NZD 100,000 minimum; secondary acquisition through named exchanges does not create the same direct account-holder relationship. Digital Cash work remains research and design, not public issuance.

An issuer-specific designation, a secondary-market token holding, a direct redemption entitlement, a registrable financial service, a licensed market service, a protected deposit and admitted settlement activity are different states.

rows.title: Entry gates
cells: Depending on the activity, gates can include FSPR registration, retail DRS membership, FMC disclosure and governance, a specified FMA or RBNZ licence, DIA-supervised AML/CFT compliance, CARF reporting status, ESAS account approval or NZClear participation. NZDD additionally depends on ECDD maintaining reserve sufficiency and public monthly verification, obtaining annual independent verification, and satisfying account-holder eligibility and compliance terms. The designation switches off during a defined period of non-compliance until remedy. FSPR registration generally involves limited checks and does not itself confer a licence.
Application, registration, licence, DRS membership, AML reporting status, prudential authorization, system admission, funding and first transaction must be tracked separately.

rows.title: Named operating actors
cells: The primary record identifies ECDD Holdings Limited as NZDD issuer, the FMA as designation maker and New Zealand registered banks as the permissible reserve-account issuers without naming the current reserve bank. RBNZ identifies ANZ New Zealand, ASB, BNZ and Westpac New Zealand as the four D-SIBs; RBNZ's 2026 stress-test description says those four account for 84 percent of lending, while ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Kiwibank and Westpac together accounted for 91 percent in the 2025 industry test. A bounded current bank-primary search located conventional deposits, open-banking payments, digital identity and risk statements, but no New Zealand-bank stablecoin, transferable deposit token, customer crypto custody or tokenised settlement launch.

ECDD, the unnamed reserve bank, a token holder, an exchange, and the major banks are different legal persons. Australian parent-bank experiments are not New Zealand subsidiary operations; ASB's historical blockchain trade window carried documents in parallel to the traditional process, not token money.

rows.title: Claims and backing
cells: The NZDD designation requires ECDD to hold NZD at least equal to the underlying currency amount of NZDD in circulation, as trustee on bare trust for holders, in a trust account whose assets are call debt securities issued by registered banks. Eligible account holders may return tokens and require NZD delivery, subject to commercially reasonable restrictions. The designation does not state that the token holder is the registered bank's depositor or that NZDD is DCS protected; only eligible covered deposits receive DCS compensation. Digital Cash would be an RBNZ-issued government-backed NZD liability if approved, while ESAS balances already are central-bank money for approved participants.

One-to-one reserve quantity, bare-trust property rights, an issuer-mediated redemption right, the bank's deposit debt, DCS eligibility, central-bank money and market-price stability are separate claims.

rows.title: Domestic rails
cells: ESAS is production RTGS infrastructure, available 23.5 hours each calendar day, with final and irrevocable settlement on simultaneous debit and credit of Exchange Settlement Accounts. Payments NZ clearing systems, SBI/SWIFT and NZClear feed it under separate access rules. NZClear provides real-time DvP model 1 securities settlement; its cash leg settles in ESAS central-bank money and the transaction is final when its last element is recorded.
Clearing instruction, exchange ledger, blockchain state, NZClear securities record and ESAS cash finality are distinct records.

groups.title: Brazil: 13 dimensions, 16 clocks, 14 gaps
groups.intro: Brazil has moved from a framework statute into an operating but transitional authorization regime. Resolutions BCB 519, 520 and 521 took effect on 2 February 2026, creating specialist intermediary, custodian and broker modalities and bringing specified virtual-asset activity into foreign-exchange rules. At the 1 October cutoff, Resolution 588 made transfers to or from self-custodied wallets at or above US$10,000 specifically reportable to Coaf, while Resolution 589 became effective only for its amendment moving the regulated-institution counterparty prohibition to 6 November; its new customer-balance, custody, proof-of-reserves and staking submissions begin 1 January 2027. CVM separately retains the securities-token perimeter. The S1 bank layer is already unevenly operational: Itaú and BTG offer direct crypto trading/custody, BTG markets its own dollar stablecoin and participates in the CSD BR fund-share mirror, Banco do Brasil offers a crypto-exposure fund and joined Caixa in current mortgage-tokenization design, while Caixa, Bradesco and Santander evidence pilots, development or announced-future products rather than a public token-money launch. Nubank is a material non-S1 retail crypto intermediary with on-chain transfers. Drex is not circulating; production finality remains in STR, SPI and Selic records.

rows.title: Authority
cells: Congress and the Presidency own the statute and decree; CMN supplies policy and prudential instruments; BCB regulates, authorizes and supervises non-security virtual-asset providers and operates STR and SPI; CVM applies securities law by represented rights; Receita owns tax and DeCripto reporting; consumer, police, prosecutors and courts own their distinct remedies.
Legislation, regulation, firm authorization, securities classification, tax reporting, system operation, investigation and adjudication are different capacities.

rows.title: Legal objects
cells: The record separates a Law 14,478 virtual asset; covered third-party service; SPSAV intermediary, custodian or broker; tokenised security; fiat-referenced virtual asset; bank or payment-account claim; simulated retail or wholesale Drex; STR reserve or settlement-account balance; SPI Conta PI balance; and Selic security position.
Digital form does not merge issuer, reserve, custodian, security right, bank liability, central-bank balance, pilot token or tax object.

rows.title: Permitted activities
cells: Covered third-party exchange, transfer, custody/control and issuer-offer or sale-related services require the applicable BCB state. Resolution 520 distinguishes intermediation, custody and combined brokerage. Resolution 521 applies FX and international-capital rules to specified international transfers, payment uses, self-custody transfers and fiat-referenced-asset trades. Security-token services remain subject to CVM law.
A BCB provider authorization does not include securities activity, central-bank account access, every affiliate or every cross-border purpose.

rows.title: Entry gates
cells: New specialist providers require BCB authorization before operation. Qualifying legacy providers may operate only through the formal transition and authorization process. Existing BCB-regulated institutions face activity-specific communication and waiting rules. Resolution 589 moved the date after which BCB-authorized institutions must not enable virtual-asset operations with non-authorized provider counterparties to 6 November 2026; the amended wording and BCB transition process must be read together rather than treating continuing operation as a final approval. CVM, STR, SPI, Pix, Selic and Drex retain separate legal-person, product, account, technical, liquidity or pilot-participation gates.
Communication, legacy eligibility, application, in-process status, final authorization, counterparty cut-off, product permission, system admission, funding and first transaction are separate clocks.

rows.title: Named operating actors
cells: BCB's March 2026 prudential segmentation places BB, Bradesco, BTG Pactual, Caixa, Itaú and Santander in S1. Their verified digital-asset states differ: Itaú offers app-based BTC, ETH and USDC trading with bank custody; BTG offers crypto trading/custody, markets BTG Dol and is the fund manager named in the CSD BR mirror; Banco do Brasil distributes a crypto-exposure fund and, with Caixa and cooperatives, signed the September mortgage-tokenization development agreement; Caixa, Bradesco and Santander have Drex or tokenization pilot/development evidence but no reviewed public token-money launch. Nubank, though not S1, is a material retail intermediary whose current terms cover buy, sell, swap, custody and selected on-chain transfers. A cutoff SPSAV cohort by CNPJ and final/in-process state remains unavailable.

S1 membership, brand, conglomerate, Brazilian legal person, bank licence, SPSAV modality, securities-fund exposure, direct virtual-asset custody, stablecoin issuer, Drex pilot node and settlement participant are different roles.

rows.title: Claims and backing
cells: For fiat-referenced virtual assets offered by in-country providers, Resolution 520 requires review and disclosure of issuer, fiat or same-sovereign public-debt reserves, custody, audited material and available redemption or reserve-claim mechanisms, and bars algorithmically controlled reserves. These remain private issuer and reserve claims. Drex pilot units are simulated; STR and SPI balances are central-bank money; a tokenised security carries its own underlying legal right. In the CSD BR project, the permissioned XRPL MPT is a complementary representation of selected deposited fund shares, while CSD BR's system remains the official record.

Disclosure and reserve eligibility do not prove one-to-one reserves, direct customer title, stress redemption, deposit insurance, legal tender or a sovereign guarantee; an MPT mirror does not displace the named official CSD record.

rows.title: Domestic rails
cells: STR is the production RTGS backbone settling in BCB Reserve and Settlement accounts; SPI settles Pix transfers in Conta PI accounts; Selic owns federal-security book entries. STR and SPI settlements are irrevocable and unconditional under their rules. Private provider books and DLT records form a separate operational layer. The CSD BR arrangement adds a permissioned public-XRPL query and audit representation of selected BTG Pactual fund shares while CSD BR retains the official registration, deposit and settlement record. Drex remains a simulated pilot with no end-user participation.
Final central-bank-money, Selic or XRPL settlement does not itself settle, validate or reverse a different system's asset record, cash leg, customer entitlement or provider-ledger entry.

rows.title: Operating state
cells: The framework law and BCB designation are effective. The detailed provider, custody and FX rules have been effective since 2 February 2026; data reporting began 4 May and DeCripto coverage began for July transactions. On 1 October, the US$10,000 self-custodied-wallet Coaf communication rule became effective and the 6 November counterparty cut-off amendment entered the rulebook. Resolution 589's new balance, custody, proof-of-reserves and staking submissions remain scheduled for 1 January 2027. Bank operating states range from live direct trading/custody at Itaú, BTG and Nubank, through fund exposure at BB, to design agreements and pilots at BB, Caixa, Bradesco and Santander. CSD BR and Ripple report live use of permissioned XRPL MPTs for a selected-fund record mirror; Drex Phase 2 is closed with its report pending.

cells: Resolution 520 supplies controls aimed at stress: cash and virtual-asset separation, proof-of-reserve methods, independent assurance, position histories, cyber controls, delisting and withdrawal procedures, non-algorithmic reserve requirements and foreign-custody safeguards. Resolution 589 will require verifiable reserve and staking totals in BCB submissions from 1 January 2027. Current Itaú, BTG and Nubank offerings create real custody and intermediary exposure, but product availability and marketing assurances do not establish customer-asset sufficiency under stress. The reviewed official sources do not provide a national cutoff-specific ledger of exchange failures, stablecoin runs, customer losses, insolvency claims or final distributions.
A preventive control or regulator's authority is not observed loss absorption, successful recovery or a government guarantee.

rows.title: Correction and loss
cells: Resolution 520 assigns scoped provider responsibility for agreed settlement, asset legitimacy, transaction-data security and customer-operation records; requires individualized customer cash accounts and separation of customer virtual assets; and requires custody discontinuity and foreign-insolvency arrangements. For the CSD BR mirror, CSD BR retains participant authorization, freeze and clawback controls and its own systems remain the official record.

Segregation, a proof of reserves, MPT freeze or clawback, correction of the official CSD record, seizure, recognized claim, issuer redemption, judicial distribution and customer receipt are different remedies and clocks.

groups.title: Argentina: 13 dimensions, 19 clocks, 11 gaps
groups.intro: Argentina has an operating CNV provider regime, fully applicable to the existing registered cohort since 31 December 2025, with five activity categories, minimum capital, custody, segregation, public proof-of-reserve, audit, conduct and reporting duties. CNV Resolution 1165, published on 7 September 2026, adds a compatibility matrix across agents, crowdfunding platforms, PSAVs, markets and clearinghouses without changing the requirements or limitations of each category. This is not a general approval of crypto as money: legal tender and fiat are outside the virtual-asset definition, and the BCRA still says regulated banks may not participate directly or indirectly in offering crypto to customers while payment-account providers may not facilitate unregulated and BCRA-unauthorized digital assets. That barrier explains the major-bank evidence: Galicia's April 2022 crypto launch was superseded by the May 2022 restriction; Banco Nacion says it is building capability for when the framework permits; Santander's Agrotoken lending work reached a pilot but not a verified current launch; and no live direct crypto product was located at BBVA Argentina or Banco Macro. Global-parent products cannot be attributed to the Argentine subsidiaries. The CNV tokenised-securities sandbox remains separate and keeps the authorized traditional security and depositary/holder-of-record chain behind its digital representation. MEP and Transferencias 3.0 are production fiat rails; no current official CBDC issuance or live pilot was located.

rows.title: Authority
cells: Congress and the Presidency enacted Law 27,739; CNV registers, regulates, supervises and sanctions PSAVs and applies securities law to tokenised securities; BCRA regulates banks, payment-account providers, FX and payment systems and operates MEP; UIF applies AML/CFT/FP; ARCA owns tax information; courts and security forces own investigation, seizure and adjudication.
Statute, provider registration, bank/payment regulation, FX access, AML reporting, tax reporting, settlement operation, seizure and adjudication are different legal capacities.

rows.title: Legal objects
cells: The record separates virtual assets, five PSAV service categories, private stablecoin claims, customer assets held in custody, fiat bank/payment-account balances, tokenised securities and their traditional deposited counterparts, and central-bank settlement balances. Legal tender and fiat currency are excluded from the virtual-asset definition.
A digital label or common platform does not merge issuer liability, customer title, custody, the traditional security, the holder of record, the depositary position or final-money entry.

rows.title: Permitted activities
cells: CNV Categories 1-5 cover fiat-to-virtual-asset exchange, virtual-asset exchange, transfer, custody/control and specified issuer-offer/sale services. Natural persons may perform only Categories 1 and 2. Mere issuance, self-trading, ordinary merchant receipt, qualifying decentralized protocols without an identifiable provider and self-custody-only wallets are outside the cited PSAV definition; securities and BCRA-regulated activities retain their own perimeters.
An exclusion from PSAV registration is not a general exemption from securities, consumer, tax, criminal, FX or other law.

rows.title: Entry gates
cells: Covered providers must register before operating and identify the exact categories. Foreign providers face local-structure and nexus tests. Minimum net worth is US$150,000 for Categories 1, 2 and 4, US$75,000 for Category 3 and US$35,000 for Category 5, with a specified 50% reduction below US$2.5 million rolling transaction/custody thresholds. AML registration, governance, custody, systems, audit and reporting requirements apply separately.
Registration, exact category, BCRA permission, foreign nexus, AML status, technical operation and current compliance are separate gates.

rows.title: Named operating actors
cells: CNV publishes a JavaScript-backed PSAV register and accepts registrations/cancellations through TAD. The reviewed static surface did not yield a reliable cutoff export of exact legal persons, categories, suspensions and cancellations; a crawler's zero result is not treated as the cohort count. The BCRA's current entity list and major-private-bank group supply the bank perimeter, while its present crypto page retains the operating restriction. Banco Nacion, Galicia, Santander Argentina, BBVA Argentina and Banco Macro were reviewed as the major-bank layer. Galicia's own 2022 disclosure records a short-lived purchase, sale and custody launch before the BCRA restriction; Banco Nacion's 25 September 2026 statement describes capability-building pending permission; Santander's Agrotoken work reached a pilot; no current direct crypto trading, custody, deposit token or bank-issued stablecoin was verified at those five institutions.
Brand, foreign parent, local company, registered category, bank or payment participant, historical launch, pilot, capability build and current operating service are not interchangeable.

rows.title: Claims and backing
cells: Category 4 PSAVs must publish proof of reserves, separate customer virtual assets and fiat from own property, keep customer virtual assets outside PSAV assets and refrain from own-account use. No reviewed official source created a dedicated stablecoin issuer reserve, direct par-redemption, recognized-token or sovereign-guarantee regime. In the tokenised-securities sandbox, the traditional authorized security and its ADCVN deposit remain behind the digital representation.
Custodian asset coverage, stablecoin issuer reserves, holder redemption, security ownership, deposit insurance and state guarantee are distinct claims.

rows.title: Domestic rails
cells: MEP is BCRA's production high-value electronic payment system; accepted transfers that pass validation and funds checks are irrevocable. Transferencias 3.0 supplies production 24/7 immediate retail transfers and interoperable QR payments over CBU/CVU accounts. PSAV books and blockchains are separate execution/custody records. Tokenised securities must remain synchronized with the conventional deposited security.
Central-bank settlement, instant account credit, PSAV execution, blockchain confirmation, customer title and securities registration are different records.

rows.title: Cross border routes
cells: PSAV fiat exchange and transfer categories, estimated stablecoin use and Argentina's FX context show that cross-border conversion is relevant. No reviewed bundle proves a recurring country pair through exact payer, beneficiary, providers, funding, FX, token transfer, final-money receipt, scale, failure and correction.
Household demand, exchange-control context, aggregate volume or provider capability is not a verified bilateral route; the map therefore carries zero arcs.

rows.title: Operating state
cells: The CNV PSAV rule is fully applicable, CNV/UIF registration and reporting are operating, and CNV's September compatibility matrix clarifies which regulated roles may be combined without relaxing the underlying requirements. BCRA's crypto-related bank and payment-provider restrictions remain on its current page. Galicia's historical bank-app crypto launch therefore is not current operating evidence; Banco Nacion's capability build and Santander's commodity-token collateral pilot remain pre-production states. MEP and Transferencias 3.0 are production fiat rails. The tokenised-securities regime is an active controlled sandbox through 31 December 2027. No current official Argentine CBDC issuance or live pilot was located.

Effective law, registered provider, compatibility, BCRA permission, discontinued historical product, pilot, capability build, operating payment rail, controlled sandbox, authorized digital representation, transaction and public production are separate states.

rows.title: Scale

No public cutoff CNV administrative aggregate was located. BCRA separately reported national 2025 payment transactions equal to 3.9 times GDP, with instant payments 64% of value and 102% of GDP.
A third-party value-received estimate is not users, balances, net flows, settled FX or government administrative data; conventional fiat-payment scale is not crypto adoption.

rows.title: Stress
cells: The rules address potential stress through segregation, public proof of reserves, custody/key controls, immutable transaction records, annual systems audit, continuity and backup, complaint handling, suspension and cancellation. The Galicia sequence is an observed regulatory correction: the bank disclosed a 27 April 2022 launch and the BCRA imposed the sector restriction on 5 May. It does not by itself disclose customer unwind, prices, transfers, losses or final custody disposition. The reviewed official bundle does not supply a national provider-failure, stablecoin-run, custody-shortfall or customer-loss series.
Required controls and risk warnings are not evidence that a firm survived stress or that customers recovered.

rows.title: Correction and loss
cells: Correction may require provider books, blockchain control, compensating transfer or issuer action, bank/payment procedures, CNV suspension, security-record reconciliation, law-enforcement seizure and court distribution. A national seizure protocol exists, while public incident-to-distribution evidence remains open.
Technical reversal, ledger correction, asset freeze, seizure, confiscation, insolvency recognition and victim restitution are separate clocks; MEP finality does not make a crypto claimant whole.

rows.title: Evidence boundary
cells: The baseline uses enacted law, current compiled CNV rules, official CNV/UIF/BCRA/ARCA publications and institution-authored bank materials. An institution's own product or annual-report statement proves only what that legal person says occurred; absence from a bounded current-product search is not a guarantee of no private experiment. BBVA group services in Switzerland, Spain or Europe are not attributed to BBVA Argentina, and Santander group work outside Argentina is not treated as a local product. groups.title: South Africa: 13 dimensions, 19 clocks, 12 gaps
groups.intro: South Africa has an operating but layered crypto-service regime: the FSCA licenses covered FAIS advice, intermediary and investment-management services; FIC Item 22 and Directive 9 impose separate AML and travel-rule duties; SARS applies tax and CARF reporting; and SARB and FinSurv retain currency, exchange-control and settlement authority. Crypto is not legal tender or SARB-backed, and a dedicated prudential stablecoin-issuer regime still was not located. The private market is nevertheless operating. BlockTower, not Standard Bank, is the issuer of the live rand stablecoin ZARU; Standard Bank holds bank-deposit reserves and provides securities custody while Sanlam manages the money-market portion. A 31 July agreed-upon-procedures snapshot reported 52.946 million ZARU in circulation, R53.717 million of eligible reserves and 101.46% coverage, but no audit opinion or assurance conclusion. Standard Bank separately reports more than R1 trillion through its Aroko blockchain-enabled conventional cross-border processing rail. Absa markets a current institutional digital-asset custody service using Ripple technology. Nedbank's planned ZAR/USDC conversion, liquidity and daily-net-settlement arrangement remains a conditional phased rollout with no reviewed production receipt. The six current systemically important banks are Absa, Standard Bank, FirstRand, Nedbank, Investec and Capitec; their states range from live custody or reserve-banking to pilots, preparation and bounded negative results. SAMOS remains final central-bank money. Khokha 2 was a proof of concept, retail CBDC is not being implemented immediately, and the August cross-border Crypto Assets Manual remained a proposal after its 30 September comment deadline.

rows.title: Authority
cells: Parliament, the Minister of Finance and National Treasury own law and policy; FSCA licenses and supervises covered FAIS crypto services; SARB, the Prudential Authority and FinSurv own banking, currency, exchange control and settlement; FIC owns AML/CFT/FP; SARS owns tax and CARF; courts and tribunals own adjudication.
Financial-services authorization, AML registration, bank prudential status, exchange-control permission, tax reporting, settlement operation and adjudication are different capacities.

rows.title: Legal objects
cells: The record separates the FAIS-defined crypto financial product, FIC Item 22 CASP activities, private stablecoin claims, custody and provider books, rand bank balances, legal tender, SAMOS central-bank money, tax-reportable crypto assets and experimental Khokha 2 wCBDC, bank token and tokenised debenture records.
A common digital interface does not merge issuer liability, direct redemption, customer title, custody, tax characterization, legal tender or final central-bank money.

rows.title: Permitted activities
cells: Covered advice, intermediary and investment-management services require FAIS authorization. FIC Item 22 separately covers client-facing fiat/crypto and crypto/crypto exchange, transfer, safekeeping/control and specified issuer-offer services. Ownership or use is not made legal tender, and cross-border activity remains subject to exchange-control permission.
Lawful possession, financial-service authorization, CASP AML status, bank access, exchange-control permission and successful operation are separate propositions.

rows.title: Entry gates
cells: A covered provider must join the exact legal person and service to an FSCA FSP authorization or representative status, fit-and-proper and conduct duties, FIC Item 22 registration and AML controls. Banking/payment access and any FinSurv permission or individual allowance remain additional gates.
Application, approval, exact activity, current compliance, bank account, authorized-dealer processing, technical availability and transaction execution are separate clocks.

rows.title: Named operating actors
cells: SARB reported 310 FSCA-licensed CASPs at 31 March 2026. Its Tether scale figure names Luno, VALR and AltCoinTrader only as the three measured platforms. SARB currently designates Absa, Standard Bank, FirstRand, Nedbank, Investec and Capitec as systemically important banks. In that bank layer, Standard Bank provides ZARU reserve banking and securities custody and operates Aroko; Absa markets institutional digital-asset custody; Nedbank has announced a conditional Crypto.com ZAR/USDC rollout; Absa, FirstRand, Nedbank and Standard Bank were active Khokha 2 participants; Investec participated in the broader project work and describes sandboxed capability; Capitec supplies risk warnings but no reviewed digital-asset product. FSCA publishes regulated-entity search surfaces, but this pass did not establish a cutoff export joining every legal person, service category, condition, suspension and active domain.

SIFI designation, a dated CASP licence count, brand, group, bank legal person, FSP, stablecoin issuer, reserve account, custodian, technology vendor, proof of concept and production service are different roles.

rows.title: Claims and backing
cells: Crypto is not SARB-issued, backed or guaranteed, and no dedicated prudential stablecoin-issuer licence was located. ZARU is a current private issuer structure: Loop South Africa, trading as BlockTower, is the issuer and FSP; Standard Bank holds cash and deposit reserves and provides securities custody; Sanlam Investment Management holds or manages the money-market portion; and Moore performs monthly agreed-upon procedures. The 31 July snapshot reported R23.314 million of cash and bank deposits plus R30.403 million of money-market funds against 52.946 million ZARU. Direct mint and redemption are limited by the whitepaper to verified institutional clients; retail or other holders use authorized partners. The report says Loop is the bank account holder and fund investor, so a token holder has an issuer redemption claim rather than a bank deposit in their own name. Khokha 2 wCBDC and bank tokens were experimental liabilities inside a proof of concept.

FSP authorization, asset custody, issuer debt, reserve account title, reserve-asset custody, direct redemption, agreed-upon procedures, deposit insurance and sovereign guarantee are distinct claims; the AUP report is not an audit or assurance opinion.

rows.title: Domestic rails
cells: SAMOS is SARB's production RTGS and supplies final and irrevocable settlement when funds or eligible collateral support the instruction. PayShap is a production fast-retail payment layer. CASP books and blockchain transactions are separate records, while SADC-RTGS is a conventional regional fiat rail.
Retail speed, bank credit, central-bank finality, CASP execution, chain confirmation, custody and customer title are different records.

rows.title: Cross border routes
cells: Directive 9 carries travel-rule information for covered domestic and cross-border transfers; existing FinSurv rules govern allowances and exchange control; and the August 2026 Crypto Assets Manual proposes a future authorized-CASP framework. Its 30 September comment deadline passed without a reviewed final instrument by the cutoff. Standard Bank's Aroko is genuine recurring blockchain-enabled cross-border bank processing with more than R1 trillion since inception, but its public description is an automated conventional FX-payment and standing-settlement-instruction rail, not a stablecoin or crypto transfer. Nedbank's ZAR/USDC route is announced and conditional, not yet supported by a production receipt. None proves a crypto country-pair route through payer, beneficiary, funding, FX, token transfer, final receipt, failure and correction.
Reporting duty, policy proposal, provider capability, aggregate activity or a regional fiat rail is not an observed country-pair route; the map carries zero arcs.

rows.title: Scale
cells: SARB reported 310 FSCA-licensed CASPs at 31 March 2026 and almost R27 billion of Tether on-chain transactions across Luno, VALR and AltCoinTrader for the year to 30 April 2026, with Silver Sixpence as the data source. ZARU's 31 July AUP snapshot reported 52,946,200.12 tokens in circulation and R53,716,955.21 of eligible reserves, a 101.46% ratio. Standard Bank reports Aroko processed more than R1 trillion since inception; its 2023 report had identified 21,682 conventional cross-border transactions worth R114 billion that year. The 2024 payment report separately disclosed PayShap use. No public complete national CASP or stablecoin settlement aggregate was established.

Licence count is not active firms; three-platform private-source volume is not a national total; a one-time issuer AUP snapshot is not continuous solvency or redemption performance; Aroko bank-processing volume is not crypto or stablecoin volume.

rows.title: Stress
cells: SARB judged crypto and stablecoin activity not currently systemic while monitoring growth, cross-border links and regulatory gaps. FSCA/FIC authorization, inspection, risk management, records and travel-rule controls are prospective safeguards. ZARU's AUP report reconciled the July snapshot above par but disclaimed any audit opinion, assurance conclusion or internal-control testing; management remained responsible for supply, circulation and reserve definitions. Absa describes hardware-protected authorization, deterministic key derivation and recoverability, but no public customer count, assets under custody, outage or recovery test was located. The reviewed bundle does not supply a national provider-failure, stablecoin-run, custody-shortfall or consumer-loss series.
A systemic-risk judgment, inspection, control or warning is not evidence of firm solvency, stress survival, quantified customer loss or recovery.

rows.title: Correction and loss
cells: Correction can involve CASP books, blockchain control, bank procedures, FinSurv regularization, FSCA/FIC action and court or tribunal disposition. FinSurv's 10%-40% settlement mechanism concerns exchange-control contraventions; SAMOS finality governs the accepted fiat entry. Neither mechanism makes a failed crypto claimant whole.
Technical reversal, record correction, license action, regulatory settlement, asset freeze, seizure, insolvency recognition and customer restitution are separate clocks.

groups.title: Nigeria: 13 dimensions, 18 clocks, 12 gaps
groups.intro: Nigeria has an enacted SEC capital-market perimeter, a July 2026 inter-agency coordination order, controlled VASP banking access, conditional SEC incubation and an applications-open CBN stablecoin sandbox. These are different states. The eNaira is operating legal-tender central-bank money and Access Bank currently provides a bank-account funding and withdrawal gateway to the CBN wallet. cNGN is a separate private claim issued by WrappedCBDC: SEC re-admitted the company to ARIP on 2 July 2026 under conditional approval-in-principle after the displayed 2024-25 test period ended. Its terms promise 1:1 naira mint and burn, deny government backing and deposit insurance, and treat retail holders as non-customers who depend on merchant or exchange channels. The exact reserve banks, current reserve report, direct institutional claims and insolvency treatment remain unproved. The May 2026 IMF report reproduced an issuer-origin estimate of about 66 million cNGN held by roughly 20 addresses, showing real but nascent scale. CBN's December 2024 stability report identified five D-SIBs without naming them; the last reviewed named official list is older, so this wave does not pretend the current five are known. Major-bank evidence is strongest for Access Bank's eNaira integration and conventional PAPSS route; no direct bank-issued stablecoin, crypto trading or custody product was verified at Access, FirstBank, UBA, Zenith or GTBank. RTGS supplies final central-bank settlement; NIP gives fast customer value before deferred net settlement. The CBN stablecoin sandbox remains applications-open and no bilateral crypto route is proved.

rows.title: Authority
cells: The Presidency and July 2026 Virtual Asset Council coordinate policy without replacing mandates. SEC owns virtual and digital assets within investment and securities business; CBN owns naira, banks, payments, settlement, eNaira and the announced non-security payment and stablecoin perimeter; NRS owns tax; NFIU and law enforcement own their financial-intelligence and enforcement functions; courts and tribunals adjudicate.
Coordination, classification, statutory jurisdiction, entity registration, payment authority, tax administration, enforcement and adjudication remain separate capacities.

rows.title: Claims and backing
cells: eNaira is direct CBN liability and legal tender. cNGN is a private WrappedCBDC liability under conditional SEC ARIP AIP. Current issuer terms promise minting only against naira deposits and one-to-one redemption after token burn for verified users, but say retail holders are not WrappedCBDC customers and the token is neither government-backed nor deposit-insured. The issuer says reserves sit in approved commercial banks but does not name the exact account banks or publish a cutoff reserve report on the reviewed surface. An IMF report reproduced about 66 million cNGN across roughly 20 addresses from an issuer-origin source. No reviewed final instrument established a general private-stablecoin issuer licence joining reserve composition, segregated custody, attestation, direct holder claim, run management and insolvency. Sandbox application requirements test such controls but do not certify an issuer or coin.

CBDC sovereign liability, bank deposit, issuer AIP, private stablecoin backing, reserve account title, merchant redemption, retail holder liquidity, custody and deposit insurance are different claims.

rows.title: Domestic rails
cells: CBN RTGS is the final-money rail: the sending bank is debited and receiving bank credited in a final and irrevocable entry. NIP supplies instant beneficiary value but settles interbank obligations on a deferred-net basis. eNaira is a separate operating CBDC ledger; Access Bank's current app moves funds between a customer bank account and the CBN wallet but does not turn the eNaira into an Access deposit. cNGN uses a private issuer ledger and public blockchain records; designated VASP naira accounts and platform books add further records.
User-visible speed, bank credit, deferred net obligation, central-bank finality, eNaira transfer, exchange execution, chain confirmation and customer title are not interchangeable.

rows.title: Cross border routes
cells: ISA cross-border powers, ordinary FX rails, eNaira remittance aspirations, cNGN marketing, sandbox eligibility and the existing ADAPT/IOTA multicountry design do not establish a named recurring virtual-asset corridor. CBN's designated VASP settlement account cannot facilitate platform FX positions or transfer them to a foreign account. Access Bank's current PAPSS service is a real conventional local-currency route from Nigeria to 11 African countries with stated beneficiary credit within 120 seconds, but it is not a crypto or stablecoin leg and lacks public transaction-level failure and final-settlement receipts.

Legal power, test eligibility, message connectivity, project design or marketing is not payer funding, FX, token transfer, beneficiary receipt, final money, failure and correction; the map carries zero arcs.

cells: At 30 June 2024, CBN reported 28,460,316 eNaira onboarded customers, only 197,041 active wallets, ₦20 billion minted and ₦18.2929 billion in circulation. Those are dated CBDC administrative measures. The May 2026 IMF report describes cNGN as nascent and reproduces an issuer-origin figure of about 66 million tokens, roughly US$44,000 at the cited conversion, held by around 20 digital addresses. Access Bank's current PAPSS page identifies 11 receiving countries and beneficiary credit within 120 seconds for its conventional route. No complete current national VASP, private-stablecoin, crypto-payment or cross-border-settlement aggregate was established.

Onboarded customers are not active wallets; an issuer-origin address and supply estimate is not holders, reserve coverage, transaction volume or redemption performance; PAPSS scale and speed are not crypto or stablecoin use.

rows.title: Stress
cells: SEC's CBEX notices identify an unregistered operator, unrealistic return claims, resumed solicitation and pre-withdrawal payment demands, with enforcement involving law enforcement. Current capital, sandbox, AML, custody and incident controls are prospective safeguards. cNGN terms allocate erroneous-address and blockchain-fee risk to the user, allow suspension and confiscation for prohibited activity, disclaim government backing and deposit insurance, and cap or exclude important forms of liability. No current reserve attestation, run test or national provider-loss series was located.
A warning, investigation, capital rule or test control is not an adjudicated loss, solvency finding, recovered-asset amount or customer distribution.

rows.title: Correction and loss
cells: Correction can involve a bank or NIP dispute record, eNaira ledger, designated VASP account, provider ledger, custody or key control, blockchain entry, SEC or CBN action, freeze or seizure, and court or tribunal disposition. cNGN terms warn that blockchain broadcasts are usually irreversible, require the merchant to send to the issuer's redemption address and assign address-error loss to the user; only after burn does WrappedCBDC initiate naira return to the designated bank account. RTGS finality fixes the accepted fiat entry but does not reverse the token transfer or make a claimant whole.
Technical reversal, bank adjustment, regulatory warning, licence action, asset freeze, seizure, adjudication, insolvency claim, recovery and restitution are separate clocks.

groups.title: Kenya: 13 dimensions, 17 clocks, 10 gaps
groups.intro: Kenya has an enacted VASP Act and final July 2026 regulations. CBK owns wallets, virtual-asset payment processing, stablecoin issuance and separate FX-conversion authorization; CMA owns exchanges, brokers, investment services, offerings and tokenisation. The rules require fully backed, segregated and insolvency-remote stablecoin reserves plus par redemption within two working days, but no cutoff-specific official VASP licence export or named stablecoin issuer was located. The bank overlay is preparatory rather than a proved crypto launch: KCB describes a possible future role as transaction-, trust-account, liquidity, FX and merchant-rail bank for licensed VASPs; Co-operative Bank reports a risk/compliance assessment underway; Stanbic describes a clearer perimeter for possible partnerships, payment rails and custody-related services; and Absa Kenya reports capacity-building for virtual assets inside its custody franchise. Equity, NCBA, I&M and DTB disclose digital-banking, market-research or conventional investment activity, not a locally launched crypto product. KCB did launch a TerraPay/Mobex incoming-remittance connection on 25 September 2026, but its release proves bank-account receipt, not a stablecoin or blockchain leg. KEPSS remains the production final-money rail and licensed mobile money is a separate conventional PSP system. CBK reported 94.35 million registered mobile-money accounts and KSh728.7 billion of agent cash-in/cash-out value in July 2026; these are not unique users or crypto scale. CBDC remains monitored, and no bilateral crypto route is proved.

rows.title: Authority
cells: National Treasury owns the policy and regulations and chairs the coordination forum. CBK licenses wallets, virtual-asset payment processors and stablecoin issuers and owns currency, PSPs and KEPSS; CMA licenses exchanges, brokers, investment services, offerings and tokenisation. KRA owns tax; FRC and law-enforcement bodies retain AML and enforcement functions; courts and tribunals adjudicate. The National Treasury and CBK opened a separate draft National Payment System Policy and Bill on 21 September 2026; the policy anticipates implications for PSP licensing and remittance products that integrate tokenised or stablecoin arrangements, but it is a proposal, not current operating authority.
Policy, proposed payment-law reform, category-specific licensing, AML registration, tax reporting, PSP authorization, settlement operation, investigation and adjudication are different capacities.

rows.title: Legal objects
cells: The record separates Act-defined virtual assets and stablecoins, consumer assets, issuer reserve assets, custody and provider books, tax-reportable transactions, bank deposits, mobile-money balances, Kenya-shilling legal tender and KEPSS central-bank settlement. Central-bank digital fiat is excluded from the Act's virtual-asset definition.
A digital interface does not merge issuer liability, reserve backing, custody, bank or mobile-money claims, tax treatment, legal tender or final central-bank money.

rows.title: Permitted activities
cells: Licensed categories cover wallets, exchanges and trading platforms, payment processing, brokerage, advice, management, offerings, tokenisation, token-issuance platforms and stablecoin issuance. Offering or admitting a stablecoin to trading also requires issuer status, CBK white-paper approval and publication; virtual-asset conversion to or from foreign currency requires separate CBK authorization.
Possession, transitional operation, application, licence, category permission, white-paper approval, FX-conversion authorization and recurring production are separate states.

rows.title: Entry gates
cells: Entry turns on the exact activity and regulator, complete application and due diligence, fit-and-proper and source-of-funds review, category capital and liquidity, local bank accounts, AML/CFT/CPF, cybersecurity, consumer and continuity controls, cross-border disclosure, tax duties and any separate FX authorization. The rules apply to foreign providers targeting Kenyan consumers or deriving Kenyan economic benefit.
Application, complete-file clock, grant, commencement within twelve months, capital compliance, exact service, transition status and current operation must be proved independently.

rows.title: Named operating actors
cells: CBK's 10 August 2026 PSP directory names Safaricom PLC, Airtel Money Kenya Limited and other legal persons for conventional payment services; Safaricom is authorized to issue, process, store, send and facilitate mobile-money payments. The November 2025 CBK/CMA notice said no VASP was then licensed. No post-regulations cutoff export joining a VASP legal person to category, conditions and commencement was located. For the bank overlay, CBK's 2025 supervision report defines an eight-bank Large peer group—KCB Bank Kenya, Equity Bank Kenya, Co-operative Bank of Kenya, Absa Bank Kenya, NCBA Bank Kenya, Stanbic Bank Kenya, I&M Bank and Diamond Trust Bank Kenya. Their own current materials prove different preparation states but no locally scoped bank-issued stablecoin, direct retail crypto dealing or production crypto-custody launch: KCB maps a possible future banking-partner role; Co-op has a risk/compliance assessment underway; Stanbic identifies possible partnership, payment-rail and custody implications; Absa Kenya is building virtual-asset custody capacity; NCBA and I&M publish market research; Equity and DTB disclose digital-banking transformation without a named crypto product.

A large-bank designation, PSP licence, strategy statement, compliance assessment, research note, capacity-building programme or parent-group capability is not a Kenyan VASP or stablecoin licence, product launch, reserve mandate, customer custody balance or recurring transaction.

rows.title: Claims and backing

No named licensed issuer, coin, reserve pool, audit or redemption series was established.
A strong statutory architecture is not proof that a particular coin is licensed, backed, liquid, redeemable in practice, deposit-insured or sovereignly guaranteed.

rows.title: Domestic rails
cells: KEPSS is CBK's production RTGS and its rules make accepted settlement final and irrevocable. Licensed mobile-money providers and other PSPs supply conventional retail payment records. The 21 September draft NPS reform seeks wider interoperability and expressly anticipates stablecoin- or token-integrated payment products, but it does not make a virtual-asset book final central-bank money. VASP books, custodial wallets, stablecoin ledgers and public blockchains remain separate records from KEPSS settlement.

A draft interoperability policy, customer-visible speed, mobile-money value, bank credit, VASP execution, chain confirmation, stablecoin redemption and final central-bank settlement are not interchangeable.

groups.title: Ghana: 13 dimensions, 18 clocks, 11 gaps
groups.intro: Ghana has enacted Act 1154, but full operationalisation remains in progress. Bank of Ghana and SEC divide VASP supervision, FIC retains AML functions, and the SEC names 20 legal persons in a controlled virtual-asset sandbox. Sandbox participation is expressly not a full licence; Bank of Ghana's application and fee pages remained unavailable after their stated end-Q3 2026 target, while the Governor described full operationalisation as a 2027 objective. The latest official virtual-asset risk assessment documents the pre-licensing bank stance: banks and PSPs were directed not to facilitate crypto transactions, filed suspicious-transaction reports, flagged or closed crypto-linked accounts, and referred some cases onward. That is observed control activity, not a current bank-by-bank product census or proof that every bank follows an identical policy. An asset-based review of Ecobank Ghana, GCB, Stanbic Ghana, Absa Ghana, Fidelity Bank and Zenith Bank found no locally scoped stablecoin issuance, crypto custody, exchange link, tokenised deposit or direct crypto dealing product. GCB's G-Money is conventional e-money; Fidelity's eCedi role was a completed pilot; Stanbic's crypto article is thought leadership; Absa's live custody offering names conventional assets. GoldBod's bank financing is conventional and its gold tokenisation is planned for 2027, while Ghana Gold Board and Africoin Ghana remain sandbox actors. Stablecoin issuance is regulated but no complete reserve or redemption regime was established. GIS supplies final central-bank settlement; GIP and mobile money are conventional retail rails. eCedi remains concluded pilot and continuing design, not production. No bilateral crypto route is proved.

rows.title: Authority
cells: Parliament and the Minister responsible for Finance own law and policy. Bank of Ghana owns currency, banking, payments, GIS and its VASP categories; SEC owns capital-market virtual-asset services and the sandbox; FIC owns financial-intelligence and AML/CFT/CPF functions; GRA owns tax; courts and tribunals adjudicate. The Virtual Assets Coordinating Committee coordinates without replacing these mandates.
Coordination, legislation, category supervision, sandbox permission, AML status, tax administration, payment operation and adjudication are different capacities.
