No cutoff notice proving a participant's transition to a full activity licence was located. Ghana has not yet published a named D-SIB roster: Bank of Ghana says the framework is being designed for a 2026-2028 implementation roadmap. The major-bank overlay therefore uses the latest explicit asset-ranked population—Ecobank Ghana, GCB, Stanbic Ghana, Absa Ghana, Fidelity Bank and Zenith Bank—and finds no locally scoped crypto launch among them. GCB operates conventional G-Money; Fidelity participated in the concluded eCedi pilot; Stanbic published recommendations; Absa's live custody and licences remain conventional.

A named sandbox participant and pilot activity are not a full licence, unrestricted public operation, completed issuance, solvency finding or endorsement. Asset rank is not D-SIB designation, and conventional e-money, CBDC-pilot participation, commentary or securities custody is not a live crypto product.

cells: Stablecoin issuance is a regulated activity, but virtual assets are not cedi, government-guaranteed, deposit-insured or covered by a statutory compensation fund. Ghana Gold Board is testing a gold real-world-asset custody role and Africoin Ghana a gold-tokenisation activity in the sandbox, while GoldBod separately says a fractional-ownership tokenisation programme is planned for 2027. Its US$75 million commercial-bank financing and self-funded gold aggregation are conventional funding and inventory arrangements, not token reserves. No general final stablecoin holder-claim, reserve, attestation, par-redemption or insolvency regime was established.
Regulatory scope and discretionary safeguards do not prove that a named coin is issued, fully backed, directly redeemable, liquid, insured or sovereignly guaranteed.

Sandbox disclosures separately warn of total or partial loss, cyberattack, key loss and potentially irreversible technology failures. groups.title: Hong Kong: 13 dimensions, 23 clocks, 11 gaps
groups.intro: Hong Kong has two separate live digital-asset licensing regimes: SFC licensing for centralised virtual-asset trading platforms and HKMA licensing for specified fiat-referenced stablecoin issuers. The official lists still establish 13 licensed VATP operators and two stablecoin issuers, but the issuer operating states have diverged. Anchorpoint Financial Limited's HKDAP entered institutional Beta Access on 12 August, completed a first trade-finance transaction and enterprise B2B settlement workflows, and at 23 September reported HK$1,006,890 in circulation against HK$2,110,045 of unaudited reserves, including HK$1.1 million of issuer-funded overcollateralisation. Independent attestations remain deferred to Full Launch. Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) is Anchorpoint's parent and largest shareholder, reserve manager, reserve custodian and first bank distributor; it separately operates tokenised deposits and institutional crypto custody. HSBC's FRS02 RedCoin remains advertised for a future 2026 launch, although HSBC already operates corporate tokenised deposits, retail Gold Token and Orion digital-bond infrastructure. The five current D-SIBs—HSBC, BOCHK, Standard Chartered Hong Kong, Hang Seng and ICBC Asia—occupy different issuance, custody, tokenisation, CBDC and conventional roles. On 29 September the Government priced about HK$20 billion of digital green bonds, with the HKD tranche incorporating tokenised-deposit settlement through EnsembleTX for the first time; that is a transaction receipt, not general 24/7 central-bank-money operation. The 16 September Policy Address targets tokenised central-bank-money settlement and 24/7 EnsembleTX operation around year-end. e-HKD remains wholesale development, not general retail issuance. HKD CHATS and FPS retain statutory finality for conventional money, and no complete recurring bilateral crypto corridor is proved.

rows.title: Authority
cells: The Legislative Council and HKSAR Government own legislation; FSTB owns financial-services policy; HKMA owns currency, banking, stablecoin-issuer licensing, payment-system oversight, Ensemble and e-HKD; SFC owns VATP, intermediary and securities-product regulation; IRD owns tax; the Stablecoin Review Tribunal and courts own distinct review and adjudication functions.
Policy, legislation, licensing, prudential supervision, product conduct, tax reporting, tribunal review, judicial adjudication and settlement-system operation are different capacities.

rows.title: Legal objects
cells: The record separates HKD and central-bank settlement balances, conventional and tokenised bank deposits, stored value, e-HKD, HKDAP and RedCoin issuer claims, stablecoin reserve trusts, VATP and bank custody, tokenised fund or gold ownership interests, digital securities, intermediary books and public-chain entries.
Digital form or common use of DLT does not merge sovereign money, commercial-bank liability, private issuer claim, investment product, custodied asset, chain record or final settlement entry.

rows.title: Permitted activities
cells: SFC-licensed VATPs may operate centralised exchange and ancillary custody within SFO, AMLO and licence conditions. HKMA licensees may issue only specified stablecoins authorised by their licences. Regulated intermediaries may provide Relevant Stablecoin services under the May 2026 conduct framework. HKDAP is operating in limited Beta Access through authorised distributors; HSBC RedCoin remains pre-launch. EnsembleTX permits scoped real-value tokenised-deposit activity inside its controlled pilot, and the September government bond used that pilot in the HKD primary-issuance settlement process.
VATP licence, issuer licence, intermediary permission, token admission, custody, controlled pilot and unrestricted recurring production are not interchangeable.

The current D-SIB roster names HSBC, BOCHK, Standard Chartered Hong Kong, Hang Seng and ICBC Asia; only the exact legal person's locally evidenced role is attributed.

rows.title: Claims and backing
cells: A specified-stablecoin holder has a par-redemption right, ordinarily within one business day after a valid request. Reserve assets must support outstanding obligations, be segregated and protected through effective trust arrangements; insolvency rights include pro-rata reserve-pool disposal and a shortfall claim against the issuer. HKDAP's whitepaper identifies Anchorpoint as debtor, Ethereum as its initial chain, Standard Chartered Hong Kong as reserve manager and intended custodian, Standard Chartered Trustee as trustee for non-digital reserve assets, and a wholesale authorised-distributor model. At 23 September Anchorpoint's weekly unaudited statement reported HK$1,006,890 in circulation and HK$2,110,045 of reserves, of which HK$1.1 million was issuer-funded overcollateralisation. Independent attestations had not begun. HSBC says RedCoin will be fully backed by segregated liquid assets and redeemable one-for-one, but the product remained future-tense.

A statutory claim, whitepaper, unaudited issuer statement and supervisory rule do not prove continuous reserve sufficiency, an independent attestation, liquidity under stress or a completed redemption; issuer equity-funded overcollateralisation is not additional circulating customer money.

Customer-visible credit, VATP execution, tokenised-deposit transfer, chain confirmation, stablecoin redemption, FPS payment and final RTGS entry remain distinct clocks and records.

rows.title: Cross border routes
cells: Payment Connect is a conventional FPS-to-Mainland real-time remittance link. Ensemble has conducted or planned sandbox and CBDC-infrastructure experiments with France, Brazil and Thailand. HSBC's production Tokenised Deposit Service completed a Hong Kong-Singapore transaction in 2025 and HSBC and Standard Chartered completed the first live cross-border tokenised-deposit interoperability transaction on Swift's blockchain ledger in August 2026, but the obligations were matched and netted before final settlement through existing systems. HKDAP's first trade-finance transaction and B2B use cases demonstrate token settlement but do not disclose a fully joined country-pair route. Circle and Tazapay describe a CPN capability that can receive USDC, convert it to HKD or USD and push funds to local Hong Kong banks, but do not identify a completed Canadian-origin transaction, local payout legal person, beneficiary credit or final-money record. No complete recurring crypto corridor is joined end to end.
A country pair, conventional payment link, DvP link, pilot, technical integration or bank product is not a sourced crypto route; the map carries zero arcs.

rows.title: Operating state
cells: VATP and stablecoin-issuer licensing regimes are effective; HKDAP is in limited institutional and corporate Beta Access, while HSBC RedCoin remains pre-launch. HKD CHATS and FPS are production rails. EnsembleTX is a controlled real-value pilot that has settled tokenised-deposit transactions and was incorporated into the HKD tranche of the fourth government digital green bond. The e-HKD pilot programme concluded; the Policy Address targets tokenised central-bank-money settlement and 24/7 EnsembleTX operation around year-end, but no cutoff receipt proves that upgrade or general retail e-HKD issuance.

Effective regime, licensed entity, beta access, public retail launch, controlled pilot, real-value transaction, production rail and general-purpose central-bank-money issuance have different operating states.

rows.title: Scale
cells: Current official lists establish 13 licensed VATPs, two stablecoin issuers and seven EnsembleTX tokenised-deposit banks. HKDAP's issuer dashboard at 23 September reported HK$1,006,890 in circulation, HK$2,110,045 in reserves, 95,010 of transaction volume, and 510,086 issued versus 66,061 redeemed over the preceding 30 days; the figures are issuer-reported and unaudited. The fourth government digital green bond was priced at about HK$20 billion across four currencies, but only its HKD primary-issuance process incorporated tokenised deposits. HSBC reported more than US$1 billion of Gold Token traded value by its 2025 results presentation and Orion reports over US$8.3 billion of digitally native bonds enabled globally. Official monthly data total 867,964,657 HKD FPS transactions worth about HK$8.62 trillion in 2025. No complete administrative series establishes VATP customers or volume, all stablecoin redemptions, EnsembleTX throughput or e-HKD adoption.

Licence and participant counts are not users or balances; issuer-reported beta metrics are not audited continuous solvency; whole-bond notional is not tokenised-deposit value; product and platform scale are not national crypto totals; conventional FPS scale is not crypto or tokenised-money scale.

rows.title: Evidence boundary
cells: The baseline uses current official HKMA, SFC, FSTB, IRD, HKICL, government, issuer and bank sources, and joins existing Workbench owners only as bounded context. It uses the five-bank HKMA D-SIB roster rather than an impressionistic big-bank list, does not attribute group activity without local evidence, and labels licensing, Beta Access, public launch, live bank products, controlled pilots, conventional rails and scheduled upgrades separately. groups.title: China: 13 dimensions, 14 clocks, 9 gaps
groups.intro: Mainland China does not operate a general licensed crypto market. The February 2026 eight-agency notice, which expressly repealed the 2021 notice, prohibits core virtual-currency business and unapproved RWA tokenization while preserving only exact authority-approved activity on specified financial infrastructure and imposing outbound controls. The separate e-CNY system moved to a 2.0 liability model on 1 January 2026: commercial-bank wallet balances are liabilities of the operating bank with interest, reserve treatment and deposit insurance, while nonbank wallet balances are provider liabilities backed by 100% guarantee funds; PBOC retains top-layer rules and infrastructure. The six large state-owned banks are both domestic systemically important banks and original operating institutions, but their customer and route evidence differs: CCB reports 30.05 million active personal wallets, 2.61 million active corporate wallets and 930,000 active merchants for 2025; PSBC reported more than 33 million wallets by mid-2025; ICBC, BOC, CCB, BoCom and PSBC disclose distinct smart-contract or cross-border receipts. BOC's July 2026 first-batch Singapore CBETS retail transactions correct the earlier signature-only state, but do not supply a complete payer-to-beneficiary finality chain. Private crypto remains prohibited. No route arc is authorized.

rows.title: Authority
cells: The NPC and State Council own primary law and administrative regulation. PBOC governs money, e-CNY top-layer infrastructure, payment systems and AML; NDRC owns mining controls; CSRC, NFRA and SAFE own securities/RWA, prudential/payment and foreign-exchange capacities within their remits; public-security, procuratorial and judicial bodies own investigation, adjudication, seizure and recovery. Digital RMB operating centers and bank/nonbank operators perform distinct infrastructure and customer-facing roles.
Legislation, policy notice, infrastructure operation, operator approval, payment-system participation, criminal process and a completed transaction are separate capacities.

Public infrastructure, digital form or shared technology does not merge central-bank money, a bank deposit, provider liability, cryptoasset, asset-backed token or settlement entry.

rows.title: Permitted activities
cells: Domestic fiat/crypto and crypto/crypto conversion, central-counterparty dealing, pricing/intermediation, token issuance and crypto financial products are prohibited, as are financial and payment services for them. Domestic RWA tokenization is prohibited unless the competent authority approves use of specified financial infrastructure. Offshore RMB-linked stablecoin issuance and specified offshore virtual-currency or RWA activity by mainland-controlled persons require Chinese consent, filing or supervision. e-CNY and conventional regulated payment activity proceed through separate approved operators and systems.
A narrow authority-gated tokenization exception, offshore licence or ordinary bank/payment licence cannot be generalized into a mainland VASP permission.

CBETS, mBridge/Jisr, CIPS and Payment Connect each require their own participant, account, liquidity, FX and use-case admissions.
Approval, system connection, preparation, contract signature, technical launch, first transaction and recurring production are separate clocks.

cells: PBOC had approved 30 bank-class e-CNY operators by 18 August 2026: the six large state-owned banks, China Merchants Bank, Industrial Bank, MYbank, WeBank, 12 banks added in April and eight added in August. The six large banks—ICBC, ABC, BOC, CCB, Bank of Communications and PSBC—also appear in the 2025 domestic systemically important bank list. New cohorts must finish preparation before service. Bank-specific evidence establishes that all six original operators have customer wallet or e-CNY application states, while BOC, ICBC, CCB, BoCom and PSBC disclose specific cross-border or smart-contract receipts. Digital RMB operating centers own domestic/international infrastructure; CBETS names 26 initial direct participants and BOC completed the first batch of Singapore retail transactions. CIPS reported 210 direct and 1,619 indirect participants at June 2026.

rows.title: Claims and backing
cells: A commercial-bank e-CNY wallet is an account-based liability of that bank, may earn interest, enters its reserve base and receives deposit-equivalent insurance treatment. A nonbank wallet is the provider's liability backed by 100% e-CNY guarantee funds. Deposit insurance currently pays covered principal and interest up to CNY 500,000 per depositor aggregated at one insured institution, with excess claims in liquidation. Private virtual-currency losses may be self-borne when the civil act violates public order, while criminal tracing and restitution remain separate.
PBOC governance, bank liability, provider liability, required guarantee funds, deposit insurance, liquidation claim, criminal seizure and actual victim recovery are not interchangeable protections.

rows.title: Domestic rails
cells: PBOC's large-value payment system and other conventional systems supply central-bank and bank-money processing; Q3 2025 large-value volume was 103 million transactions worth CNY 2,502.01 trillion. CIPS is a separate production cross-border RMB system. e-CNY 2.0 supplies bank/provider wallets under PBOC infrastructure, while Payment Connect links mainland bank infrastructure to Hong Kong FPS. groups.title: United Arab Emirates: 13 dimensions, 16 clocks, 11 gaps
groups.intro: The UAE has a layered regulatory architecture rather than one crypto licence: CBUAE owns payment tokens, Digital Dirham and licensed financial activities regardless of technology; SCA owns the federal investment-type VASP perimeter; VARA covers Dubai outside DIFC; DFSA covers DIFC; and FSRA covers ADGM. The live CBUAE register still names three Dirham Payment Token Issuance legal persons, while VARA's live register still shows 56 active fully licensed VASPs in its own Dubai perimeter. AE Coin, Zand AED and DDSC have product evidence; DDSC has one disclosed AED 110 million transaction. The major-bank layer is uneven: FAB is a DDSC founding participant and proposed customer-access channel but AEDC Stable Coin LLC is the registered issuer; Emirates NBD's Liv X operates retail crypto brokerage through VARA-licensed Aquanow with Zodia custody; ADCB has VASP risk controls but no verified customer crypto product; and DIB's Crypto.com work remains an exploratory MoU. Digital Dirham has bounded live government and UAE-China CBDC transactions, not proven general public circulation. UAEFTS remains the sovereign RTGS/finality anchor. No map route arc is yet authorized.

rows.title: Authority
cells: Federal law and Cabinet decisions establish the national frame. CBUAE owns payment-token services, Digital Dirham, technology-neutral licensed-financial-activity jurisdiction and payment-system oversight. SCA owns federal investment-type VAs and VASPs outside financial free zones. VARA covers Dubai outside DIFC, DFSA covers DIFC and FSRA covers ADGM. FTA owns tax; courts, insolvency office-holders and law enforcement own separate adjudication and recovery capacities.
Federal, emirate, commercial-free-zone, financial-free-zone, payment-token, investment-product, tax, enforcement and settlement authorities are distinct and may overlap only through an express gate.

rows.title: Permitted activities
cells: CBUAE licences AED-token issuance and licences or registers payment-token conversion, custody and transfer. SCA, VARA, DFSA and FSRA licence or authorise location- and activity-specific investment and VASP services. Ordinary merchants may accept licensed Dirham Payment Tokens, while registered Foreign Payment Tokens are bounded to virtual-asset or derivative purchases. Algorithmic stablecoin and privacy-token issuance, service and promotion are prohibited in the CBUAE payment perimeter.
Issuer, conversion, custody, broker, exchange, advisory, market, merchant-payment and promotion permissions attach to exact legal persons, activities, instruments and territories.

rows.title: Entry gates
cells: Payment-token issuance requires a CBUAE licence; conversion and foreign-token custody may require CBUAE non-objection on top of SCA or local VASP status. VARA in-principle approval cannot operate or serve clients. DIFC and ADGM require their own DFSA or FSRA authorisation. Register inclusion and exact activity scope establish entry, not an application, marketing claim or group-company licence.
Application, IPA, non-objection, licence grant, effective date, product approval, launch, first transaction and recurring production each require separate evidence.

rows.title: Named operating actors
cells: The live CBUAE register names AED StableCoin L.L.C - S.P.C, Zand Trust L.L.C S.O.C and AEDC Stable Coin-L.L.C as Dirham Payment Token Issuance legal persons and AEDC Stable Coin Network And Distribution - L.L.C in conversion/custody and payment-service categories. VARA's cutoff register shows 56 active fully licensed VASPs in Dubai outside DIFC. AE Coin, AEDZ and DDSC have named product evidence. CBUAE's latest explicit public D-SIB population is FAB, Emirates NBD, ADCB and DIB; Zand is reviewed separately because its trust company is a registered issuer. Other federal and financial-free-zone rosters still need a joined cutoff export.
Legal person, group, licence, licence category, product brand, agent, network, active customer service and market scale are different facts.

rows.title: Claims and backing
cells: Payment-token holders have a par-redemption right without delay and no later than the same time on the next business day unless CBUAE permits otherwise. The default reserve is 100% same-currency cash in segregated escrow; a bank-owned issuer may hold at least 50% cash and the remainder in short-duration UAE government bonds or CBUAE M-bills. Daily reconciliation/reporting, monthly external audit and an insolvency claim against the reserve are required. Issuer-specific current balances and redemption performance remain open.
Statutory design, product statement, dated reserve balance, attestation, liquidity, redemption request, completed payment and insolvency recovery are separate evidence states.

The bank-product review verifies Liv X retail crypto trading, with Aquanow providing brokerage infrastructure and Zodia custody; it does not make Emirates NBD the exchange or custodian. groups.title: Switzerland: 13 dimensions, 17 clocks, 10 gaps
groups.intro: Switzerland regulates crypto-related activity through existing functional financial-market perimeters plus the 2021 DLT legislation, not one general crypto licence. FINMA-authorised banks and securities firms, the regulated SIX digital securities infrastructure and the first DLT trading facility supply named institutional entry points. The SNB has issued wholesale CBDC for live production-environment settlement on SIX since December 2023 and extended the bounded Helvetia pilot through at least June 2028; BX Digital separately uses a production SIC RTGS link with traditional central-bank money. All four systemically important banking groups participate in the controlled CHFD stablecoin sandbox, but they do not thereby become issuers: Swiss Stablecoin AG provides issuance infrastructure and CHFD Infrastruktur AG operates the platform. Separately, UBS has live tokenised-securities and fund workflows but no active spot-crypto offer on its cited product page; ZKB directly custodies bitcoin and ether while Crypto Finance executes trades; PostFinance offers 22-asset trading, custody and ETH staking with Sygnum; and no broader Raiffeisen customer crypto product was verified. Stablecoins remain private repayment claims and the sandbox is not a public launch. No permanent CBDC, retail CBDC or recurring cross-border route is established, so the map carries no route arc.

rows.title: Authority
cells: The Confederation defines the Swiss franc; the SNB owns central-bank money, SIC rules and payment-system oversight; FINMA owns prudential, conduct and FMI licensing; FINMA-recognised SROs supervise many AML-only financial intermediaries; tax, courts and insolvency authorities retain separate roles. The 2021 DLT Act adapted existing law rather than creating a single crypto regulator.
Currency, prudential licence, conduct, AML membership, market-infrastructure approval, tax, adjudication and insolvency distribution are separate authorities and states.

rows.title: Legal objects
cells: The record separates coins and banknotes, SNB sight deposits, commercial-bank deposits, Helvetia wholesale CBDC as a technical representation of SNB sight deposits, payment tokens, utility tokens, asset tokens, ledger-based securities, stablecoin issuer claims, custodied cryptobased assets and settlement entries. Hybrid-token rules may be cumulative.
A shared token or ledger form does not merge sovereign money, bank liability, issuer debt, investment right, custody asset, securities record or final cash settlement.

rows.title: Permitted activities

DLT facilities may conduct qualifying multilateral DLT-securities trading and specified custody or clearing/settlement functions. The proposed dedicated payment-instrument and crypto-institution categories are not current law at the cutoff.
Technology, marketing, token issuance, SRO membership and one licence category do not authorize all services or instruments.

SIX operates regulated digital-securities CSD infrastructure; BX Digital is the sole listed DLT trading facility. Nine banks are currently eligible for Helvetia wCBDC, but eligibility does not establish usage by each bank.
Legal person, group, ordinary licence, crypto-facing service, product admission, technical connection and active transaction are distinct facts.

rows.title: Claims and backing
cells: FINMA says stablecoin holders generally hold an at-any-time payment claim against the issuer; classification normally follows public-deposit or collective-investment law depending on whose account and risk the backing is managed for. A bank default guarantee can remove funds from the deposit definition but carries conditions and residual issuer, holder and guarantor risks. The participating banks are not automatically co-issuers. Helvetia wCBDC is an SNB liability; commercial deposits and custodied cryptoassets follow different protection paths.
Legal design, guarantee, reserve asset, dated balance, attestation, liquidity, redemption request, completed payment, deposit insurance and insolvency recovery are separate evidence states.

rows.title: Operating state
cells: The DLT legal framework, SDX/CSD infrastructure, SIC and instant payments are effective and operational. Helvetia wCBDC has been used for live production-environment settlement since December 2023 and now runs through at least June 2028 as a pilot. BX Digital holds an effective licence and the SNB describes its RTGS link as productive. CHFD became technically live inside a controlled sandbox at the end of June 2026 and entered a nine-company use-case test phase on 8 September; the test has restricted participants and limits and is not a public product or market decision. Dedicated stablecoin and crypto-institution licences remain proposed, and no retail or permanent wholesale CBDC is established.
Effective law, licence, technical readiness, production connection, bounded pilot, first transaction, recurring operation and permanent policy adoption are not interchangeable.

groups.title: France: 13 dimensions, 18 clocks, 11 gaps
groups.intro: France implements MiCA through the AMF and ACPR while Banque de France and Eurosystem infrastructure retain the public-money settlement spine. The major-bank layer is already heterogeneous and material: Société Générale-FORGE issues live EURCV and USDCV; Crédit Agricole group company CACEIS Bank issues live EURXT and used it for a first tokenised-fund subscription; BPCE subsidiary Hexarq provides direct retail crypto trading and custody through 13 network banks; BNP Paribas provides indirect BTC/ETH exposure through six ETNs and separately completed a controlled intra-group tokenised-fund experiment; Banque Fédérative du Crédit Mutuel is a Qivalis consortium member while that proposed issuer remains unauthorised; and no comparable production crypto or token-money product was verified for La Banque Postale. These are separate issuer, CASP, securities and development states. On 21 September 2026 the Eurosystem launched Pontes, with Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and Société Générale among the initial onboarded participants, but no France-specific completed Pontes transaction, recurring volume or exception record is yet established. No substantive French legal, licence, product or settlement change was found after 22 September through the intraday cutoff; no route arc is authorised.

rows.title: Authority
cells: The EU supplies MiCA; French law allocates national powers among the AMF, ACPR and Banque de France. AMF owns French CASP authorisation and conduct, ACPR owns prudential and French EMT-issuer authorisation, Banque de France owns the national central-bank and TARGET layer, and FGDR, courts and insolvency authorities own separate protection and adjudication functions.
EU rule, national implementation, prudential licence, market conduct, central-bank operation, guarantee payout and adjudication are separate authorities and states.

rows.title: Named operating actors
cells: ACPR's six-principal-group comparison identifies BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Groupe Crédit Agricole, Groupe BPCE, Groupe Crédit Mutuel and La Banque Postale; the first four were 2024 G-SIBs. Exact operating legal persons differ inside those groups. Société Générale-FORGE issues EURCV and USDCV and is an EMI, investment firm and CASP. CACEIS Bank, the Crédit Agricole asset-servicing bank, is a notified credit-institution CASP and issues EURXT. Hexarq SAS, a BPCE subsidiary, is the licensed retail CASP. BNP Paribas' French commercial bank distributes securities-based crypto exposure while its asset-management, Securities Services and AssetFoundry units performed the tokenised-fund experiment. Banque Fédérative du Crédit Mutuel is a Qivalis member, not the proposed issuer. Circle France remains a separate non-major-bank EMT issuer.
Group, issuer, bank, CASP, distributor, transfer agent, tokenisation platform, custodian, CSD, central bank and system operator must remain exact legal persons and roles.

cells: T2 settles payment transactions individually in central-bank money with irrevocable and unconditional finality; T2S supplies securities settlement in central-bank money; TIPS supplies instant settlement; ESES France uses simultaneous gross securities transfer and central-bank-money cash settlement. Pontes launched on 21 September 2026 as a DLT-to-TARGET interface, with CDC and Société Générale among the initial onboarded participants. Effective law, issuer licence, current supply, product availability, securities exposure, customer crypto custody, completed transaction, controlled experiment, consortium membership, system operation, participant readiness and design roadmap are not interchangeable.

groups.title: Canada: 13 dimensions, 15 clocks, 11 gaps
groups.intro: Canada still uses overlapping AML, retail-payment, securities, banking and payment-system regimes rather than one crypto licence. The post-15 September changes are concrete but narrow: a 16 September multi-jurisdiction decision let Netcoins add Solana to cryptoassets exempt from specified investment limits, and on 22 September all six Canadian D-SIBs announced only an exploration of interbank Canadian-dollar tokenised deposits. No common token, issuer, ledger, customer launch, first transfer, finality rule or production scale was disclosed. BMO separately planned a U.S.-dollar institutional tokenised-cash/deposit platform for H2 2026 pending approval and joined Project Agorá on 29 September; TD disclosed a real-value Agorá transfer, but it was between U.S. legal entities, not a Canadian production route. Q3 Pillar 3 returns show that the banks' present crypto activity is mostly capital-markets intermediation, collateral/repo, brokerage and custody rather than deposit-token issuance: RBC disclosed CAD1.920 billion held under custody but only CAD3 million on-balance-sheet plus CAD28 million off-balance-sheet exposures subject to its simplified-approach deduction, while BMO, CIBC, National Bank, Scotiabank and TD disclosed heterogeneous and often substantially hedged Group 2 books. The Stablecoin Act remains enacted but not in force and expressly targets non-financial issuers; bank-issued tokenised deposits remain prudentially regulated bank liabilities. Lynx remains the production Bank-of-Canada-books final-money anchor, RTR was still scheduled for Q4, and no retail CBDC is issued.

rows.title: Authority
cells: Parliament and the Governor in Council own federal law and commencement; the Bank of Canada owns central-bank money, system oversight, RPAA supervision and the future stablecoin regime; FINTRAC owns AML registration and supervision; provincial and territorial regulators coordinated through CSA own securities and crypto-platform decisions; Payments Canada operates core systems; CDIC, courts and insolvency authorities own separate protection and recovery functions.
Enactment, commencement, registration, licensing, supervision, system operation, insurance and adjudication are different capacities.

rows.title: Legal objects
cells: The record separates Canadian-dollar central-bank money, each bank's own deposit liability, a possible tokenised representation of that liability, RPAA end-user funds, AML-defined virtual currency, crypto contracts, value-referenced cryptoassets, future Stablecoin Act objects and USDC as a private issuer claim. Finance Canada says the future Stablecoin Act is for non-financial issuers because banks and credit unions already sit inside comprehensive prudential regimes.

A tokenised deposit remains a claim on the named deposit-taking bank unless the design creates a different legal object; digital form or a common dollar reference does not merge public money, insured deposit, safeguarded funds, platform contract, stablecoin claim or chain entry.

rows.title: Scale
cells: The first comparable quarterly OSFI templates expose bank intermediation but not one market-size measure. At 31 July 2026: RBC reported CAD1.920 billion market value under custody, excluded from its capital requirement, alongside CAD3 million on-balance-sheet and CAD28 million off-balance-sheet exposures under the simplified approach; BMO reported Group 2a long CAD11 million, short CAD10 million and CAD7 million capital requirement; TD reported CAD46 million long, CAD23 million short, CAD10 million capital requirement and CAD1 million Group 2b deduction; CIBC reported Group 2a long and short CAD93 million, plus CAD2 million Group 2b and CAD2 million deduction, with CAD378 million assets and CAD212 million liabilities in its CAE2 accounting table; National Bank reported Group 2a RWA CAD150 million, long CAD181 million, short CAD184 million and CAD6 million capital; Scotiabank reported Group 2a long and short CAD35 million and CAD8 million capital, plus accounting balances heavily shaped by crypto-related repo liabilities. These consolidated prudential snapshots differ by method and include hedges, collateral, repo, derivatives, securities and client-broker balances; they do not identify Canadian customers or tokenised-deposit use. The record still lacks national customers, stablecoin circulation, redemptions, payments and corridor volumes.

Custody assets, gross longs, shorts, risk-weighted assets, accounting assets/liabilities, deductions and capital requirements are different measures; none alone establishes beneficial ownership, customer geography, payment volume, issuer solvency or corridor scale.

groups.title: Rwanda: 13 dimensions, 17 clocks, 11 gaps
groups.intro: Rwanda now has an effective virtual-asset statute, but the reviewed official record does not yet show an operational licensing market. Law No. 023/2026 was gazetted and entered into force on 28 May 2026. It makes the Capital Market Authority the primary virtual-asset regulator, preserves a National Bank of Rwanda role over monetary stability and payments, requires licences or issuer approval, prohibits natural persons from carrying on virtual-asset business, treats virtual assets as non-legal-tender, and bars their direct use for payments unless NBR authorizes it. Stablecoins require prior CMA approval, full collateralization, liquid reserves, professional custody, audit and insolvency segregation; algorithmic stablecoins are excluded from the statutory virtual-asset category. Yet CMA's current regulation, application and licensee pages show no implementing virtual-asset regulation, VASP application route, VASP category, stablecoin issuer or approved virtual-asset product. The law is therefore effective while the public entry-and-authorization layer remains unproved. Rwanda's major banks remain conventional deposit, payment, securities-custody and cross-border-banking institutions: Bank of Kigali, BPR, I&M, Equity, Ecobank and Access disclose ordinary digital channels or regional transfers, but no reviewed primary source proves a Rwandan bank-issued stablecoin, tokenized deposit, crypto custody service, VASP licence or real-value token settlement. The e-FRW is still a proof of concept, and the Ghana-Rwanda passporting framework remains permission architecture rather than a transaction receipt.

rows.title: Authority
cells: Parliament owns statutes. Law No. 023/2026 makes CMA the virtual-asset Regulatory Authority, including licensing, issuer and product approval, inspection and rulemaking. NBR retains currency, payment-system, banking, e-money, PSP, financial-stability and CBDC authority and, under the new law, collaborates on monetary-stability, payment and systemic-risk matters and alone may approve direct virtual-asset payments. FIC owns financial-intelligence and AML/CFT/CPF functions; courts adjudicate offences and insolvency questions.
Statute, implementing regulation, CMA licence, CMA issuer approval, NBR payment authorization, bank supervision, AML supervision and adjudication are different acts by different authorities.

rows.title: Legal objects
cells: Law No. 023/2026 covers transferable or tradable digital value used for payment or investment, real-world tokenized assets and reserve-backed stable-value assets. It excludes digital fiat representations, NBR-regulated payment instruments, capital-market instruments, CBDC, closed-loop value, purely private non-trading value, NFTs, enhanced-anonymity assets and algorithmic stablecoins. The wider record separately preserves FRW cash, NBR settlement balances, bank deposits, e-money, safeguarded PSP funds, securities, covered virtual assets and a possible future e-FRW liability.

A statutory virtual asset, excluded algorithmic stablecoin, tokenized security, bank deposit, e-money claim, central-bank balance and CBDC are not interchangeable; exclusion from this law can mean another regime applies, not that the object is approved.

rows.title: Permitted activities
cells: A CMA-licensed legal entity may provide the services enumerated in Article 14, including issuance/listing/trading platforms, clearing or settlement, fiat or virtual-asset exchange, transfer, order execution, placement, custody or administration, escrow, advice and investment management. Issuance, trading or listing of a virtual asset requires prior CMA approval; stablecoins have additional Article 19 duties. Natural persons may not conduct virtual-asset business. Virtual assets are not legal tender and may not be used directly to pay for goods, services, debts or financial obligations unless NBR authorizes that use. Mining facilities, crypto ATMs and mixers or tumblers require authorization.

An activity named in effective law is not presently permitted to a person without the required licence or approval; statutory possibility, filed application, authorization, launch and first transaction remain separate.

sources.label: Law No. 023/2026 regulating virtual asset business

rows.title: Entry gates
cells: Article 10 requires a legal entity incorporated or registered in Rwanda with local presence, beneficial-owner disclosure, fit governance, regulatory capital and AML controls; regulations must prescribe procedures and capital. As of the cutoff, CMA's regulations page did not list a virtual-asset implementing regulation, its application page did not offer a VASP route, and its licensee page showed no VASP or approved issuer category. A June CMA procurement for virtual-asset consultancy indicates implementation work, not a licence window. Payment services still require the exact NBR licence, while Ghana passporting requires home permission, a Letter of No Objection and joint governance.

An effective framework law can coexist with an unproved implementing gateway; consultancy, awareness, application, home licence, no-objection letter, host permission, technical connection and first transaction are distinct clocks.

rows.title: Named operating actors
cells: NBR's supervised-bank list names nine commercial banks—Bank of Kigali, BPR Bank Rwanda, I&M Bank Rwanda, GT Bank, Ecobank Rwanda, Access Bank Rwanda, Equity Bank Rwanda, BOA Rwanda and NCBA Rwanda—plus BRD and ZIGAMA CSS. NBR says five unnamed D-SIBs held 75.6% of banking assets at December 2024, so this record does not invent a name-to-D-SIB mapping. Bank of Kigali, BPR, I&M, Equity, Ecobank and Access form the bank operating sample. CMA separately lists Bank of Kigali, BPR and I&M as traditional capital-market custodians, not virtual-asset custodians. The current CMA roster names no VASP, stablecoin issuer or approved virtual-asset product. NBR's November 2025 list names 42 conventional PSP entities; the Ghana-Rwanda pilot's four firms remain unnamed.
A bank, parent group, securities custodian, PSP, VASP, issuer and cross-border pilot participant are different legal and operating roles; a parent's activity elsewhere is not Rwandan-bank activity.

rows.title: Claims and backing
cells: Article 19 requires an approved stablecoin to be 100% collateralized at all times, bars lending reserve assets for yield, requires independent-auditor confirmation of liquidity for reasonable and timely redemption, verification means, a licensed professional custodian, regular audits and segregation from issuer and creditor assets for insolvency. Further regulations may still determine reserve-investment conditions. E-money remains a separately regulated redeemable issuer claim backed by at least equivalent authorized currency and safeguarded through trust or equivalent mechanisms; bank deposits remain bank liabilities subject to the DGF statute.

Statutory reserve design is not evidence that a stablecoin exists, that its assets were deposited, or that redemption worked; stablecoin reserves, e-money safeguarding, bank capital, deposit insurance and central-bank liability are separate protections.

cells: NBR operates clearing and settlement facilities and modernised RIPPS; eKash supplies interoperable national P2P payments while mobile-money and bank PSPs supply customer interfaces. Current detailed RIPPS and eKash finality, exception and participant-default rulebooks were not retrieved.
Customer display, PSP ledger, e-money transfer, eKash instruction, clearing and final NBR settlement are different records and clocks.

rows.title: Cross border routes
cells: The Ghana-Rwanda licence-passporting framework was signed in February 2025, approved in October 2025 and piloted with two PSPs from each country. It establishes a permission pathway but does not identify the firms, exact permissions or a completed payment. I&M's BRISK offers near-real-time USD, KES, TZS and UGX transfers among I&M entities and Ecobank markets conventional regional transfer products; neither is a crypto or token-settlement route. The e-FRW proof of concept only simulated cross-border flows and calls for a later live pilot with one partner central bank.

Mutual recognition, conventional correspondent or intragroup transfer, a Letter of No Objection, interoperability planning and simulated flow do not prove a cryptoasset, stablecoin or CBDC crossed a border; no crypto route arc is authorized.

rows.title: Operating state
cells: Law No. 023/2026 is effective, but the public implementation layer remains incomplete or unproved: no virtual-asset regulation, application route, VASP licence, stablecoin issuer approval, bank token product or transaction appears in the reviewed CMA/NBR pages. The payment and e-money regimes, licensed PSPs, eKash and ordinary bank digital channels operate. Bank of Kigali's Open API concerns account checks, payments and bill settlement; BPR's and CMA's custody evidence concerns conventional securities; I&M and Ecobank cross-border products are fiat banking. The e-FRW remains a completed proof of concept rather than issued CBDC.
Effective statute, implementing rule, open gateway, licensed actor, approved product, technical launch, first real-value transaction, recurring operation and issued CBDC are distinct states.

rows.title: Scale
cells: NBR reported 11 banks with FRW8.7 trillion of assets at December 2024 and five unnamed D-SIBs holding 75.6%. Bank-level public scale confirms a concentrated conventional system: Bank of Kigali reported Q1 2026 loans of FRW1.745 trillion and deposits of FRW1.895 trillion; BPR reported 2025 assets of FRW1.405 trillion and customer deposits of FRW874.0 billion; Ecobank reported 2025 assets of FRW636.9 billion and deposits of FRW552.2 billion. By June 2025, eKash had 20 onboarded institutions, 2.16 million active users and 25 million monthly transactions worth FRW105 billion. FIC identified nine commonly accessed VASPs, but no administrative VASP-license, stablecoin-reserve, bank-token, virtual-asset customer, balance or transaction series was found.
Bank assets, deposits, PSP count and e-money traffic measure conventional finance; they are not crypto custody, tokenized deposits, stablecoin reserves or CBDC adoption.

sources.label: Monetary Policy and Financial Stability Statement March 2025
BPR Bank 2025 Integrated Report and Financial Statements
2024 National Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment

rows.title: Stress
cells: FIC's assessment records high virtual-asset financial-crime risk and unregulated access. The new law requires reporting of fraud, theft, complaints and remedies, transaction tracing, cyber controls, continuity and freeze compliance, but no public administrative series yet demonstrates those controls in operation. Access Bank Rwanda's AML page classifies cryptocurrency dealers among prohibited businesses, a bank-specific risk policy rather than national law. NBR reports D-SIB resolvability assessments and a crisis simulation for banks; the CBDC proof of concept identifies privacy, cyber, device, failed-transaction and lost-credential risks. No primary-source national virtual-asset failure, custody shortfall, bank-token incident, loss or recovery series was located.
Risk assessment, bank client policy, statutory control, supervisory exercise, observed incident, quantified loss, judgment and distribution are separate evidence states.

sources.label: 2024 National Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment
Law No. 023/2026 regulating virtual asset business
Annual Report 2024–2025 — crisis management and resolution
Rwanda CBDC Proof of Concept Report

rows.title: Correction and loss
cells: The virtual-asset law allows a competent authority to order freezes for substantiated suspected illegality, sanctions or investigations; requires VASPs to safeguard customer assets, preserve originator and beneficiary records, screen addresses and report fraud, theft, complaints and remediation; and places unauthorized business, issuance, marketing, payments, mining facilities, ATMs and mixers under criminal penalties. Stablecoin reserves must be insolvency-segregated. Separately, payment-law safeguards, bank-resolution powers and the DGF protect different conventional claims. No reviewed evidence shows a licensed VASP insolvency, stablecoin redemption, customer-asset distribution or freeze-and-recovery case under the new law.

Address freeze, balance reduction, ledger correction, refund, safeguarded-fund claim, stablecoin reserve claim, bank resolution, deposit-guarantee payout and criminal restitution have different owners and clocks.

rows.title: Evidence boundary
cells: This recertification uses the Official Gazette law, live CMA regulation/application/licensee pages, NBR system and bank records, exact bank disclosures, FIC, Bank of Ghana and the Rwanda governor. It treats the absence of a public implementation object as a bounded negative result, not proof that CMA received no private inquiry. It does not convert CMA's conventional securities-custodian category, ordinary bank APIs or fiat regional transfers into crypto custody or token settlement, and does not attribute foreign-parent activity to a Rwandan subsidiary.
Fresh research is not Chronicle promotion, investment advice, publication authority, app shipment, proof of a licence, or proof of a crypto corridor.

sections.title: The global layer: Swift, BIS Agorá, Open USD, The Clearing House and others (6 records)
sections.sub: Swift says most of seventeen first-mover banks have used its ledger for controlled 24/7 tokenized-value payments in five currencies across six continents; exact bank pairs, values, final-settlement systems and exception records remain undisclosed. Project Agora completed thirty real-value transactions across seventeen controlled scenarios and six currencies, but remains a prototype with manual controls and without standing production integration. Open USD launched on four public networks on 30 September 2026 with Bridge identified as issuer and more than 200 partners; the first monthly attestation, reconciled supply, reserve-account ownership and stress-redemption record remain outstanding. The Clearing House selected Quant for its future tokenized-deposit network, expected in the first half of 2027; vendor selection and legacy-network scale are not launch or transaction evidence. No post-22 September FATF, FSB or Basel instrument was found that itself changes domestic law, firm permission or settlement finality. XRP Asia launched a Singapore-based regional XRPL builder hub with visible Singapore, Tokyo and Seoul community nodes and public intake. The organizational launch changes no country licence, monetary claim, bank settlement or bilateral-route state and authorizes no map arc.

sections.title: Stablecoin laws, jurisdiction by jurisdiction (9 cards, as of July 28, 2026)
sections.sub: One home for the Stablecoin Field Guide's law comparison: nine jurisdiction cards (EU, UAE, United States, Hong Kong, United Kingdom, South Korea, Japan x3) kept in the page's own words, each with the page's status line, date, category, lead, 'careful' caution, the compared fields (when, currency, who may issue, what has to back it, who may sell or hold it, how it settles, at the store checkout, currency angle) and the page's links. The chapter's own question, lede and finding are kept in chapter. No existing master covered laws outside the GENIUS Act (stablecoins.json carries only GENIUS provisions), so this file was created; the U.S. card overlaps stablecoins.json#/law_context in subject but not in wording. Evidence is as of the page's 2026-07-28 cutoff. Card src links are the page's links and have not been re-checked against the primary-source rule.
columns: Who may sell or hold it

rows.title: European Union: stablecoins need a license as e-money or asset-backed tokens
cells: Europe regulates by legal type of token. It is the clearest category-first model.
Only a credit institution or an electronic-money institution may issue an e-money token. Issuers of asset-referenced tokens need a separate authorization.
Duties on reserves, liquidity, keeping assets separate, custody and redemption at any time differ by token type. E-money token holders can redeem at face value. Paying interest on them is prohibited.
Crypto-asset service providers need an EU-wide authorization and follow EU-wide conduct rules.
The token may move on a blockchain. Issuer redemption and bank or central-bank money settle separately, each final at its own time.
MiCA authorization is not a European Central Bank (ECB) guarantee, deposit insurance, or acceptance by every merchant.

rows.title: United Arab Emirates: stores may accept only licensed dirham tokens
cells: The UAE shows that legal routing and merchant permission decide stablecoin acceptance, not contactless (NFC) capability.

A UAE company may be licensed to issue a Dirham Payment Token; a bank issues through a subsidiary or affiliate. Issuing, converting, holding and transferring foreign tokens each need their own permission.

By default, reserves are 100% cash in the same currency, held in a separate escrow account at an unrelated UAE bank. A qualifying bank-owned issuer may hold at least 50% cash and the rest in short UAE government or CBUAE instruments, with extra capital and controls.
Issuing, holding and transferring, and converting tokens are separate regulated services.
The wallet transfer is the customer's part. Reserve cash and redemption are separate parts, at a commercial bank or, when directed, in central-bank custody.
A terminal that supports contactless payment does not meet the rules on token licensing, conversion, custody, merchants or redemption.

rows.title: United States: the GENIUS Act sets who may issue and what they must hold
cells: enacted · not yet generally in effect
Of these laws, GENIUS most directly links more stablecoins to more government-debt purchases for reserves. It also shows most clearly that stablecoin law is banking law too.
Permitted issuers are subsidiaries of insured depository institutions, federal qualified issuers, or state qualified issuers, divided by the law's federal–state split and size threshold.

Reserves must match coins one-to-one: cash, central-bank balances, insured deposits, Treasury bills of 93 days or less, qualifying repurchase agreements (repo), government money funds and related liquid government assets. Issuers report monthly. Holders get no interest and no FDIC insurance.
Wallets, card networks, processors and distributors can be separate companies from the legal issuer. A restriction on service providers starts in 2028, setting a later deadline for market access.
Blockchain transfer, card-network obligation, minting and redemption, bank-deposit movement and central-bank final settlement stay separate.
Enacted does not mean in effect. A proposal, a charter application or a conditional approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) is not a live GENIUS issuer authorization.

rows.title: Hong Kong: issuing a stablecoin requires a license from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority
cells: Hong Kong uses licensing by the regulator: a strict issuer license in an international financial center.
Issuing an in-scope stablecoin tied to a government currency (fiat-referenced) in Hong Kong requires a license. So do specified issuing or offering activities linked to Hong Kong.
HKMA supervision focuses on reserve management, redemption, risk management, governance, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing (AML/CFT) controls, and disclosure.
Only specified regulated institutions may offer in-scope stablecoins to retail investors. The issuer's license and the permission to distribute are separate.
The Ordinance covers the issuer and the token's promise, not the merchant's card processor (acquirer) or the final bank-money payment.
A sandbox place, a license application or a public announcement is not a license.

rows.title: United Kingdom: issuing stablecoins becomes a licensed activity; the full regime is expected to start in late 2027
cells: Britain is the best example of a license requirement already in law whose operating rules are still being written.
Issuing a UK qualifying stablecoin becomes a regulated activity. For systemic payment stablecoins, the Bank of England adds oversight to FCA supervision.
Qualifying stablecoins are tied to a government currency and hold backing assets. Detailed FCA rules are expected to provide full backing and redemption rights.
Safeguarding and other crypto activities need separate permissions. The government is still settling what the dealing and payment-services rules cover.
The UK is explicitly designing stablecoins as both cryptoassets and possible payment instruments, with separate oversight of systemic ones.
Do not call the late-2027 regime live. Current policy notes explicitly describe more rules and payments reform still to come.

sources.label: HM Treasury — April 2026 stablecoin payments note

rows.title: South Korea: a bank-led won stablecoin is under discussion, not law
cells: Korea is the comparison case: strong technical readiness does not mean settled law.
A bank-centered model, including a debated consortium with banks holding 50%+1, was discussed, not adopted.
Not final. Existing bank-token and wholesale-settlement pilots are separate from any won-stablecoin law.
The Bank of Korea's work puts central-bank and commercial-bank money first, with stablecoins as a supplementary option.
A committee discussion or a bank proof of concept is not a won-stablecoin law.

rows.title: Japan: trust-issued stablecoins may hold up to half their reserves in short government bonds
cells: Like GENIUS, Japan lets reserves fund government debt, but more narrowly: only trust stablecoins may hold limited short government bonds.
Banks, registered funds-transfer providers, and trust companies or trust banks issue different legal claims. A lighter intermediary that holds no customer assets may broker for a full provider.

Covered trust stablecoins may hold up to 50% in qualifying government bonds of three months or less, or in term deposits that can be withdrawn early without losing principal. At least 50% stays in demand deposits. Rules on daily fair-value measurement and fixing shortfalls apply.
Full EPI providers handle sale, exchange, brokering or custody. The lighter intermediary cannot hold customer assets.
Trust redemption, deposit-token settlement, bank reserves and a public-blockchain transfer are different things. Each settles on its own timeline.
JPYSC running on controlled venues is not open-wallet circulation at merchants. Tokenized bank deposits are not trust stablecoins.

rows.title: Japan: crypto trading moves under securities law; stablecoins stay under payments law
cells: The split is the key point. Japan keeps ‘crypto,’ ‘stablecoin’ and ‘bank deposit’ as separate legal things.
This is not a new stablecoin issuer category. Stablecoins, as electronic payment instruments, stay under the PSA.
This card covers no change to stablecoin reserves.
Rules on trading, offerings, lending, management, advice, disclosure, intermediary duties and unfair trading move under the FIEA.
The law deliberately keeps market regulation separate from the settlement of payment money.
Do not say Japan made every cryptoasset a security, legal tender or a bank deposit.

rows.title: Japan: paper checks and bills to stop clearing from April 2027 (a plan, not a stablecoin law)
cells: official transition plan from industry and government
Japan is changing both ends at once. It is retiring paper claims while making new tokenized claims legal.
Banks still owe the payment; only the form of the payment instruction changes.
Electronically recorded monetary claims and internet transfers replace presenting paper.
This is a direct move from cash and checks to electronic payment systems, separate from stablecoin law.
This is an official transition plan. It is not a stablecoin law, and it does not prove every check disappears on one day.
